definition_zh: 巨大的；沉重的；大量的；严重的；体格魁梧的；块状的（岩体）；大面积的（病变）；厚重的（建筑）
definition_en: very large in size, weight or amount, often so large that it is striking or hard to deal with
core_image: 港口边立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具
scene: 港口入口立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具。 A massive block of granite now stands at the harbour entrance.
sceneCN: 这里指体积巨大、分量惊人（第 1 个义项：形体或体量极大）；句意为一块巨大的花岗岩石料如今立在港口入口处；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa「团块」，是该形容词的词基，义为「团块；大量；群众的」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地；极其」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「巨大；沉重感」
由「团块」加表示动作或集合的名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」，是建筑用语
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块；地块」，指连成整体的一组山体

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: occupying far more space than ordinary objects of its kind, so that it dominates a view
senses.definitionCN: 占据的空间远大于同类常见物体，因而在视野中占主导
senses.example: A massive crane lifted the bridge section into place.
senses.exampleCN: 一台巨大的起重机把桥段吊装到位。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant a lump or a mass, so the adjective first describes sheer bulk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为「团块、一堆」，因此这个形容词首先描述的是纯粹的体量。

senses.title: Heavy and solid
senses.definition: thick and weighty, made of material that feels hard to move
senses.definitionCN: 厚而重，由让人感到难以搬动的材料做成
senses.example: The altar is a massive slab of stone.
senses.exampleCN: 祭坛是一整块沉重的石板。
senses.why: A mass has weight as well as size, so the adjective carries both impressions at once.
senses.whyCN: 团块既有体积也有重量，因此这个形容词同时带着两种感受。

senses.title: Huge in amount
senses.definition: present in a very large quantity, said of data, sums, effort or numbers of people
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的数量存在，用于数据、金额、努力或人数
senses.example: The archive holds a massive amount of correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 这间档案馆藏有大量往来信件。
senses.why: Amounts can pile up like material, and a heap that keeps growing becomes a mass.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以像材料一样堆积，越堆越高的那一堆就成了「团块」。

senses.title: Extremely serious in effect
senses.definition: very great in severity, so that recovery or repair is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 严重程度极大，以至于恢复或修复都很困难
senses.example: The earthquake caused massive damage to the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 地震给老城造成了严重破坏。
senses.why: Damage has size too, and damage of enormous size is expressed with the word for bulk.
senses.whyCN: 破坏也有「大小」，巨大规模的破坏就用表示体量的词来表达。

senses.title: Broad and heavy in build
senses.definition: having a large, solid body, said of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 身体大而结实，用于人或动物
senses.example: A massive guard stood at the gate all night.
senses.exampleCN: 一名魁梧的守卫整夜站在门口。
senses.why: A body can have the same solid bulk as a stone block, and English applies the word to people.
senses.whyCN: 身体可以有和石块一样厚实的体量，英语便把这个词用在人身上。

senses.title: Formed as one unbroken rock body
senses.definition: in geology, said of rock that has no visible bedding or layering, appearing as one solid mass
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中用于看不出层理、呈一整块的岩石
senses.example: The cliff is cut into massive granite with no clear layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这面崖壁由无明显层理的整块花岗岩构成。
senses.why: Geology uses the word for rock that behaves as a single lump rather than as stacked sheets.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个词指表现得像一整块、而不是叠层薄片的岩石。

senses.title: Very extensive in medicine
senses.definition: said of a bleed, clot or infarct that covers a large part of an organ
senses.definitionCN: 用于覆盖器官很大一部分的出血、血栓或梗死
senses.example: He survived a massive heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 去年冬天他挺过了一次大面积心肌梗死。
senses.why: Clinical language measures lesions by extent, and an extent near the whole organ is massive.
senses.whyCN: 临床按范围量度病灶，范围接近整个器官的就称为「大面积」。

senses.title: Thick and plain in construction
senses.definition: built with heavy walls and simple, undecorated forms, often of stone
senses.definitionCN: 以厚重墙体与简洁无装饰的形式建造，常用石材
senses.example: The cathedral's massive walls were built to last centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座主教座堂的厚重墙体是为挺过数百年而建的。
senses.why: Architecture judges weight and simplicity together, and a building that shows its mass is called massive.
senses.whyCN: 建筑把重量与简洁一起评价，一座显露自身质量的建筑就被称为「厚重」。

intro.en: Massive comes from Latin massa 'lump, mass', itself from Greek maza 'barley cake', through French massif. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and geology, medicine and architecture later gave it precise uses.
intro.cn: massive 来自拉丁 massa「团块、一堆」，后者源于希腊 maza「大麦饼」，经法语 massif 进入英语，十六世纪被采用；地质、医学与建筑后来赋予它精确用法。

items.en: Maza named a kneaded barley cake, a single shapeless lump of dough, and the image of one solid mass began there.
items.cn: maza 指揉成的大麦饼，是一团没有形状的面团，「一整块实体」的画面由此开始。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass or a body of material, and it also gave English mass.
items.cn: massa 意为团块、一堆或一团材料，也给出英语的 mass。

items.en: French massif described something solid and bulky, and English took the adjective in that form.
items.cn: 法语 massif 形容坚实而笨重的东西，英语照这个形式引入形容词。

items.en: English massive first described heavy objects and bodies, then extended to amounts and effects.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先形容沉重的物体与身体，后扩展到数量与后果。

items.en: Geology uses massive for rock without bedding, and architecture for walls that display their weight.
items.cn: 地质学用这个词指无层理的岩石，建筑用指显露自身重量的墙。

items.en: Clinical writing measures an infarct or bleed by how much of an organ it covers, and a very large one is massive.
items.cn: 临床文字按覆盖器官的多少来量度梗死或出血，覆盖很大的就称为大面积。

note.en: The first group shares the lump stem; the second group holds size words that differ in scale, shape or tone.
note.cn: 第一组共享「团块」词干；第二组是表示大小的词，在规模、形状或语气上各有不同。

entries.definition: A quantity of matter, or a large number of people; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 一定量的物质，或一大群人；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: To an enormous degree; it often modifies verbs such as increase or build.
entries.definitionCN: 达到巨大程度；常修饰「增加」「建造」一类动词。

entries.definition: The quality of being huge and heavy; a state noun used in description.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而沉重的性质；是用于描写的状态名词。

entries.definition: The arrangement of volumes in a building; an architectural term from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑中各体量的组合；同一词干来的建筑术语。

entries.definition: Very big; the general word, without the suggestion of solid weight.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大；通用词，不带「坚实沉重」的暗示。

entries.definition: Extremely large; it stresses scale beyond expectation rather than mass.
entries.definitionCN: 极大；强调超出预期的规模，而非质量。

entries.definition: Large and awkward to move because of shape; it adds inconvenience to size.
entries.definitionCN: 因形状而大得难以搬动；在「大」之外多了不便。

entries.definition: Astonishingly large, as a giant statue; it carries awe rather than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 大到惊人，如巨型雕像；带惊叹意味，而非重量感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means a lump: massive things come as one solid block.
normal.cn: 词根意为「团块」：巨大的东西是一整块实心的。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massively, massiveness and massing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括团块、巨大地、巨大、体量组合。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark quantity and severity: massive amount, massive damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出数量与严重程度：大量、严重破坏。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: massive rock, massive heart attack.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：块状岩体、大面积心肌梗死。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: huge is general, bulky adds awkwardness, colossal adds awe.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：huge 是通用词，bulky 多了笨重，colossal 多了惊叹。

abstract.en: Picture a single stone so large that a road bends around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块大到公路要绕着走的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so thick that no one can cross it.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人多到没人能穿过去。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose frame alone weighs more than a car.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，光是门框就比一辆车重。

examples.en: The company made a massive investment in new machinery.
examples.cn: 这家公司在新机器上投入了巨额资金。

examples.en: A massive storm shut down every ferry in the region.
examples.cn: 一场猛烈的风暴让该地区所有渡轮停运。

examples.en: The cathedral's massive walls have stood for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座主教座堂厚重的墙已经立了六百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马四伏」——四匹马伏在一起才拉得动，形容巨大沉重

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、一团面团」→ 拉丁 massa「团块」→ 法语 massif → 英语 massive；同族 mass、massif、massing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one solid bulk: an object in space, weight in the hand, a growing quantity, the scale of damage, a body, a rock body, a lesion, or a wall.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一团实在的体量：空间里的物体、手里的重量、不断增大的数量、破坏的规模、身体、岩体、病灶，或一堵墙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shapeless lump so big that it dominates whatever stands beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大团没有形状的实体，大到让它旁边的一切都显得渺小。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE: a large object and its solid weight.
branches.cn: 物理基础：庞大的物体与其坚实的重量。

branches.en: THE QUANTITATIVE FORM: a heap of data, money or people.
branches.cn: 数量形态：一堆数据、金钱或人。

branches.en: THE SEVERITY FORM: damage on a scale that is hard to repair.
branches.cn: 严重形态：难以修复的大规模破坏。

branches.en: THE HUMAN FORM: a broad, heavy body.
branches.cn: 人的形态：宽厚沉重的身体。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL FORMS: rock without bedding, a lesion covering much of an organ, and walls that show their weight.
branches.cn: 技术形态：无层理的岩体、覆盖器官大部的病灶，以及显露重量的墙。

intro.en: Massive rests on Latin massa 'lump' and the adjective ending -ive; English adds endings for manner, state and architectural arrangement.
intro.cn: massive 建立在拉丁 massa「团块」与形容词词尾 -ive 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与建筑组合的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa 'lump' gives English mass directly; Medieval Latin massivus and French massif give the adjective massive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa「团块」直接给出英语 mass；中世纪拉丁 massivus 与法语 massif 给出形容词 massive。

items.example: The noun is the origin of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的来源。

items.meaning: a body of matter; a great number
items.example: The noun kept both the physical and social senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留物理与社会两义。

items.example: The ending makes a describing word of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成描述词。

items.example: The medieval form passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪形式经法语传下。

items.example: English extended it to amounts and severity.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到数量与严重程度。

items.example: The suffix gives the degree adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出程度副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of bulk.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「体量巨大」的性质。

items.example: The noun names a geological mass of rock.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名地质上的岩块。

items.example: The ending builds the architectural term massing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出建筑术语「体量组合」。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of growth and spending.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「增长」「开支」类动词。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa，义为「团块；大量」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「巨大」
由词根加动作名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块」

definition_zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的；军队；军方
definition_en: relating to soldiers, armed forces, or war; also, as a noun, the armed forces of a country taken as one body
core_image: 一队士兵踏着同一节奏行进，枪挎在肩，靴底压过碎石
scene: 天刚亮，一队士兵沿着山口悄悄行进，靴底踩得碎石作响。 At dawn the military column moved through the pass without a sound, rifles slung and boots crunching on the gravel.
sceneCN: 这里 military 是「军事的、军队的」（第 1 个义项：属于军队或战争的）；句意：黎明时分，这支军队的队伍悄无声息地穿过山口，枪挎在肩上，靴子踩得碎石作响。场景要点：天刚亮、狭窄山口、成列行进的士兵、肩上的步枪、碎石上传来的靴声；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的
军队；军方（与定冠词连用，the military）

collocations.zh: 军队；军方（作为一个整体）

senses.title: Of soldiers and war
senses.definition: relating to soldiers, armies, or the conduct of war in general
senses.definitionCN: 与士兵、军队或战争行为有关的
senses.example: The museum's new wing is devoted to military history.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的新展区专门展示军事史。
senses.why: Latin militaris was simply the adjective of miles, 'soldier'. Anything it described belonged to the soldier's world, and that broad belonging is still the first sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 militaris 就是 miles（士兵）的形容词。它修饰的任何东西都属于士兵的世界，这种宽泛的归属至今仍是英语里的第一个义项。

senses.title: Done by soldiers, for soldiers
senses.titleCN: 由军人执行、供军队使用
senses.definition: carried out by soldiers or intended for the armed forces, rather than merely discussing them
senses.definitionCN: 由军人执行或供武装部队使用的，而不只是谈论军队
senses.example: The old airfield is now used for military training.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧机场现在用于军事训练。
senses.why: The adjective does not only label a topic; it also marks who acts and who benefits. A military operation is planned and run by soldiers, so the word moves from 'about soldiers' to 'by and for soldiers'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不只标注话题，还标明谁在行动、谁在受益。军事行动由军人筹划和执行，于是这个词从“关于士兵”走到“由士兵做、为士兵做”。

senses.title: Soldier-like precision
senses.definition: used figuratively of behaviour that is as exact, orderly, and disciplined as a soldier's
senses.definitionCN: 比喻像军人一样精确、整齐、守纪律的行为
senses.example: She folded the map with military precision and handed it back.
senses.exampleCN: 她以军人般的精确折好地图，递了回去。
senses.why: Soldiers drill until every movement is measured and repeated. The adjective borrows that drilled exactness and lends it to civilian actions that have nothing to do with armies.
senses.whyCN: 士兵反复操练，直到每个动作都被量得准确、重复得整齐。这个形容词借来那种操练出来的精确，借给与军队无关的日常动作。

senses.title: By force, not by talk
senses.definition: describing a solution or spirit that relies on armed force or favours it
senses.definitionCN: 形容依靠武力或崇尚武力的解决办法与精神
senses.example: The dispute was settled by military means after talks failed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判失败后，这场争端以军事手段解决。
senses.why: If the soldier's instrument is force, then calling a solution military announces that force will be used. The adjective shifts from describing an institution to recommending its method.
senses.whyCN: 如果士兵的工具是武力，那么把一个解决办法称为军事的，就是在宣告将动用武力。这个形容词从描述一种机构，转为推荐它的手段。

senses.title: The whole body of soldiers
senses.definition: with the definite article, the armed forces of a country considered as one collective body
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，指一国的武装力量整体
senses.example: The military were called in to clear the roads after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，军队被调来清理道路。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by taking 'the': the military, short for the military forces. A collective noun names all the soldiers as one thing, just as the column in the core image moves as one body.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词加上定冠词就变成了名词：“the military”，是“the military forces”的省略。集合名词把所有士兵命名成一个东西，正如核心意象里的队伍作为一个整体移动。

senses.title: The military as a power bloc
senses.titleCN: 军方：作为政治权力机构
senses.definition: the armed forces viewed as an institution that can act in politics and hold power
senses.definitionCN: 把武装部队看作能够在政治中行动、掌握权力的机构
senses.example: The military seized power overnight and closed the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 军方一夜之间夺取政权，并关闭了议会。
senses.why: Once the column of soldiers acts as a single actor in public life, 'the military' stops meaning a crowd of men and starts meaning an institution with its own will and weight.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这支队伍在公共生活中作为一个单一行动者行事，the military 就不再指一群士兵，而开始指一个有自己的意志与分量的机构。

senses.title: One soldier, old-fashioned
senses.definition: in older usage, a soldier or a military man, countable and now rare
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指一名军人或军事人员，可数，现已罕见
senses.example: The old novel describes a retired officer simply as 'a military'.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小说把一名退役军官径称为“一名军人”。
senses.why: The noun first named one person, 'a military man' (1736), before it named the whole body. The singular use survives only as an archaism, a fossil of the earlier step.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词先指一个人，即“a military man”（1736 年），后来才指整个群体。单数用法只作为古语残存下来，是较早那一步的化石。

senses.title: Service in the ranks
senses.definition: in phrases such as 'in the military', the state or career of serving in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在“in the military”一类短语中，指在武装部队中服役的状态或经历
senses.example: He spent six years in the military before returning to the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他服役六年，之后回到农场。
senses.why: To be in the military is to stand inside that collective body. The core image of a formed column becomes a place a person can enter, belong to, and leave.
senses.whyCN: 身处军队，就是站进那个集体之中。核心意象里列队成形的队伍，变成了一个人可以进入、归属并离开的地方。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: used attributively to name an academic field whose subject is armies, wars, and defence
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，命名以军队、战争与防务为对象的学科领域
senses.example: She teaches military history at the war college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在军事学院教授军事史。
senses.why: The same adjective that marks soldiers' business can mark the study of that business. The object of the field is still the column, only now it is observed from a desk instead of a trench.
senses.whyCN: 标记士兵事务的同一个形容词，也可以标记对这一事务的研究。这个领域的对象仍是那支队伍，只是现在是从书桌前观察，而不是从战壕里。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective that English borrowed through French in the fifteenth century; the collective noun arrived three centuries later, and the origin of the Latin base is still unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: military 是 15 世纪经法语借入英语的拉丁语形容词；集合名词要晚三百年才出现，而拉丁语词根的来历至今没有定论。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as militari, 'pertaining to or befitting soldiers; used, done, or brought about by soldiers'. It came from Old French militaire (14c.) and directly from Latin militaris.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 militari，意为“与士兵有关或适合士兵的；由士兵使用、完成或造成的”。它来自古法语 militaire（14 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 militaris。

items.en: Latin militaris meant 'of soldiers or war, of military service, warlike'. It was formed from miles (genitive militis), 'soldier', a word of unknown origin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 militaris 意为“士兵的、战争的、兵役的、尚武的”。它由 miles（属格 militis）“士兵”构成，而这个词的来历不明。

items.en: The origin of miles is unsettled. It may be Etruscan, or it may mean 'one who marches in a troop', which would connect it to Sanskrit melah 'assembly' and Greek homilos 'assembled crowd'. De Vaan finds it tempting to link it to milia 'thousands', hence *mili-it- 'who goes with the thousand'. None of these is proved.
items.cn: miles 的来历没有定论。它可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，也可能意为“随队伍行进的人”，从而与梵语 melah“集会”、希腊语 homilos“聚集的人群”相联系。De Vaan 认为把它与 milia“数千”联系起来很诱人，即 *mili-it-“随千人同行的人”。这些说法都未被证明。

items.en: The noun first meant 'a military man' (1736). 'Soldiers generally' is recorded from 1757, and it is commonly used only with the definite article.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“军人”（1736）。泛指“士兵、军队”的用法记录于 1757 年，而且通常只与定冠词连用。

items.en: The adjective spreads into fixed phrases: military age, the age at which one becomes liable for service (1737); military police (1827); and military-industrial complex, coined in Eisenhower's farewell speech (1961).
items.cn: 这个形容词扩散到固定短语中：military age 指应服兵役的年龄（1737）；military police 即军事警察（1827）；military-industrial complex 即军工复合体，由艾森豪威尔在告别演说中铸成（1961）。

items.en: Militia is a separate borrowing: 1580s, 'system of military discipline', from Latin militia 'military service', and only from the 1690s 'citizen army'. Militarism (1841) came from French militarisme. Military is the adjective, militia the citizen body, militarism the ideology.
items.cn: militia 是另一次借入：16 世纪 80 年代指“军事训练制度”，来自拉丁语 militia“兵役”，到 17 世纪 90 年代才指“公民军队”。militarism（1841）来自法语 militarisme。military 是形容词，militia 是公民武装，militarism 是主义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin miles stem but has drifted into different jobs; the second compares the ordinary words for organized fighters.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语 miles 词干，却各自漂向不同的职责；第二组比较表示有组织武装人员的常用词。

entries.definition: a body of citizens enrolled for military service in an emergency, not professional soldiers. It is a force, while military is the adjective of the professional institution.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急时征召服役的公民队伍，不是职业军人。它是一支力量，而 military 是职业军队的形容词。

entries.definition: willing to use strong or violent action for a cause, or a person who is. It describes a stance or a person, never an army as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意为某项事业采取强硬或暴力行动的，或指这样的人。它描述一种立场或一个人，从不指整支军队。

entries.definition: the belief that a country should keep a strong military and use it aggressively. It names a doctrine, not the forces themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 认为国家应保持强大军力并积极使用武力的信念。它命名一种主义，而不是军队本身。

entries.definition: organized and armed like an army but outside the official armed forces. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the difference from regular military bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 组织与武装像军队、却处于正规武装力量之外的。前缀 para-“在旁”标出它与正规军事组织的区别。

entries.definition: the branch of a country's forces that fights on land, or a large body of soldiers. It is one service, while the military can mean all services together.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量中在陆地作战的分支，或一大群士兵。它是一个军种，而 the military 可指所有军种的整体。

entries.definition: the combined military forces of a country, including army, navy, and air force. It is the full official phrase for what 'the military' names in one word.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量的总和，包括陆军、海军与空军。它是对 the military 一词所指对象的完整正式说法。

entries.definition: soldiers, especially those serving in a particular place or operation. It counts people, while the military names an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 士兵，尤指在某一地点或行动中服役的人。它数的是人，而 the military 命名的是一种机构。

entries.definition: organized groups of soldiers, often qualified as land, air, or naval forces. It is a flexible plural, close to 'the military' but usually needs a qualifier.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的军人群体，常以陆地、空中或海上限定。它是灵活的复数，接近 the military，但通常需要限定语。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, the -ary ending, and the separate but related borrowings militia and militarism.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris、后缀 -ary，以及另行借入但相关的 militia 与 militarism。

normal.en: miles is Latin for 'soldier'; militaris is its adjective. Military begins as nothing more than 'of the soldier'.
normal.cn: miles 是拉丁语的“士兵”，militaris 是它的形容词。military 最初不过是“士兵的”。

normal.en: The adjective came first, in the fifteenth century; the noun 'the military' for soldiers as a body is recorded only in 1757.
normal.cn: 形容词先出现，在 15 世纪；把士兵作为整体来称的 the military 直到 1757 年才有记录。

normal.en: The -ary ending makes an adjective, so military, militarily, militarism and militarize all grow from the same stem with different endings.
normal.cn: -ary 结尾使它成为形容词，所以 military、militarily、militarism、militarize 都从同一词干加上不同词尾长出来。

normal.en: militia is a separate borrowing from Latin militia 'military service'; its 'citizen army' sense is only from the 1690s.
normal.cn: militia 是从拉丁语 militia“兵役”另行借入的词；它的“公民军队”义要到 17 世纪 90 年代才出现。

normal.en: The definite article matters: the military is the whole body, while a military is an old-fashioned way to say one soldier.
normal.cn: 定冠词很关键：the military 指整个军队，而 a military 是旧式说法，指一名军人。

abstract.en: Picture a column of boots striking gravel at the same instant. The sound is not many sounds but one sound repeated, and that is what makes it military.
abstract.cn: 想象一列靴子在同一瞬间踏在碎石上。那声音不是许多声音，而是一个声音的重复，正是这种重复使它成为“军事的”。

abstract.en: The adjective is a uniform that can be put on anything: a bridge, a budget, a history, a way of folding a map.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词是一套可以套在任何东西上的制服：一座桥、一份预算、一段历史、一种折地图的方式。

abstract.en: When the column stops marching and starts deciding, it becomes 'the military' — one actor with a will, not a crowd of men.
abstract.cn: 当这支队伍停止行进、开始作决定，它就变成了“军方”——一个有意愿的行动者，而不是一群士兵。

examples.en: Military spending rose for the third year in a row.
examples.cn: 军费开支连续第三年上升。

examples.en: The airfield is still under military control, and no civilian flights are allowed.
examples.cn: 这座机场仍处于军事管制之下，不允许民用航班起降。

examples.en: After the earthquake, the military was sent in to reopen the mountain roads.
examples.cn: 地震之后，军队被派去重新打通山路。

dict_mnemonic.text: “米里特力”——米里藏着一群特别有力气的壮汉，列队扛枪向前 → military 军事的；军队（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 miles“士兵”的形容词 militaris，核心是“属于士兵与军队的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of military, all growing from one picture: a body of soldiers moving as a single column, and then acting as a single institution.
sensesIntro.cn: military 的九个义项都长自同一幅画面：一队士兵作为一个整体行进，随后作为一个整体机构行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of soldiers stepping as one body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队士兵作为一个整体迈步。

branches.en: SOLDIER'S WORLD: the adjective first marks what belongs to soldiers, then what is done by them and for them.
branches.cn: 士兵的世界：这个形容词先标记属于士兵的东西，再标记由士兵做、为士兵做的事。

branches.en: BORROWED QUALITIES: drilled exactness is lent to civilian actions, and the soldier's instrument, force, is lent to solutions.
branches.cn: 借来的品质：操练出的精确被借给日常动作，士兵的工具即武力被借给解决办法。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND POLITICAL: 'the military' first names all soldiers as one body, then names that body as a power in politics.
branches.cn: 集体与政治：the military 先把所有士兵命名成一个整体，再把这个整体命名为政治中的一种权力。

branches.en: ONE MAN AND A CAREER: the old singular names a single soldier, while 'in the military' names service inside the body.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：旧式单数指一名军人，而 in the military 指在这个整体内部服役。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same adjective marks the academic field that observes armies from a desk.
branches.cn: 研究领域：同一个形容词标记从书桌前观察军队的学科。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective ending in -ary; the stem milit- also carries -ia, -ism, -ist, -istic, -ize and -ation into English. The prefix para- in paramilitary is Greek, added later.
intro.cn: military 是带 -ary 后缀的拉丁语形容词；词干 milit- 还把 -ia、-ism、-ist、-istic、-ize 与 -ation 带进英语。paramilitary 里的前缀 para- 是后来加上的希腊语成分。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words sit behind the family: miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, and militia 'military service'. The origin of miles itself is disputed, so no deeper root can be stated as fact.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族背后有三个拉丁词：miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris，以及 militia“兵役”。miles 本身的来历有争议，因此不能把更深的词根当作事实来陈述。

items.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（milit- 士兵 + -ary 形容词后缀）
items.example: The country keeps a large military budget.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家维持着庞大的军事预算。

items.meaning: in a military way; by military means
items.meaningCN: 在军事上；以军事手段（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The region is militarily important but economically poor.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区军事上重要，经济上却贫穷。

items.meaning: the belief in strong armed forces and their use
items.meaningCN: 军国主义；尚武精神（-ism 构成主义）
items.example: The book traces the rise of militarism before the war.
items.exampleCN: 这本书追溯了战前军国主义的兴起。

items.example: The general was widely seen as a militarist.
items.exampleCN: 这位将军被普遍看作军国主义者。

items.meaningCN: 军国主义的；黩武的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The parade had a strongly militaristic tone.
items.exampleCN: 这场阅兵带有强烈的黩武色彩。

items.meaningCN: 使军事化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The island was militarized during the crisis.
items.exampleCN: 危机期间，这座岛屿被军事化了。

items.meaningCN: 军事化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: People protested against the militarization of the police.
items.exampleCN: 人们抗议警察的军事化。

items.meaning: a citizen army called out in an emergency
items.meaningCN: 民兵组织；紧急时征召的公民武装（拉丁语“兵役”）
items.example: The local militia guarded the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 当地民兵守卫着那座桥。

items.meaningCN: 好战的；激进分子（-ant 构成形容词或指人）
items.example: A militant wing of the movement rejected the talks.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动的激进一派拒绝了谈判。

items.meaning: to work against something, as evidence or circumstance
items.meaningCN: 妨碍；起不利作用（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The high cost militates against any quick repair.
items.exampleCN: 高昂的成本不利于任何快速修复。

items.meaning: armed like an army but outside it
items.meaningCN: 准军事的（para- 在旁 + military 军事的）
items.example: A paramilitary group controlled the border road.
items.exampleCN: 一个准军事组织控制着那条边境公路。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（miles 士兵 + -aris 形容词后缀）
士兵（词源不明，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语）
兵役；战争（miles 士兵 + -itia 抽象名词后缀）

definition_zh: 地带；区域；时区；（将……）分成区域
definition_en: an area with a particular purpose or feature, or one of the belts into which the earth is divided
core_image: 地图上一条虚线圈起来的一块，圈内规则一样，圈外换了规矩
scene: 机场广播提醒旅客，过了安检口就进入限制区域。 Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
sceneCN: 这里 zone 是「区域」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的划出的一片地方）；句意为上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。地图上虚线围起的一块，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 zone 加 -ing 构成，义为「区划；区域规划」
由 zone 加 -ed 构成，义为「被划成区的」

senses.title: The marked area
senses.definition: an area with a particular purpose or feature, marked off from what is around it
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的或具有特定特征而划出的一片地方
senses.example: Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
senses.exampleCN: 上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。
senses.why: The word came from a Greek noun for a belt or girdle, and a belt around an area is the image behind every later use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「腰带」的名词，围住一片地方的带子就是后来各种用法的画面。

senses.title: The bands of the earth
senses.definition: one of the belts into which the earth is divided by climate, by time, or by latitude
senses.definitionCN: 按气候、时间或纬度把地球划成的带
senses.example: The earth is divided into twenty-four time zones.
senses.exampleCN: 地球被划分为二十四个时区。
senses.why: The oldest use fitted the earth itself, where a wide belt of the globe could be marked off and named.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法直接用在球体上，把地球上一圈宽带划出来命名。

senses.title: The area set aside
senses.definition: an area set aside by law or rule for one use, such as parking, building, or trade
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依规留给某种用途的地片，如停车、建筑或贸易
senses.example: The old harbour became a free trade zone last year.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港区去年成了自由贸易区。
senses.why: A marked strip of land can be reserved by rules, so the belt becomes an official zone with its own regulations.
senses.whyCN: 划出的一条地可以按规则保留，于是这条带子成了有自己的规章的正式区域。

senses.title: To divide into zones
senses.definition: to divide an area into zones, usually for building rules or planning
senses.definitionCN: 把一片地方划成若干区，多用于建筑规则或规划
senses.example: The council zoned the land for housing twenty years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在二十年前就把这片地划作住宅区。
senses.why: The noun turns into an act of drawing the belts on the map, so the same word works as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了在地图上画带子的动作，于是同一个词也能作动词。

senses.title: The space of focus
senses.definition: a state of deep attention, used in phrases such as in the zone, and in zone out for losing attention
senses.definitionCN: 高度集中的状态，见于 in the zone，以及 zone out 表示走神
senses.example: After ten minutes she was in the zone and finished the paper quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 十分钟后她进入了专注状态，很快就写完了卷子。
senses.why: A zone that encloses an area also encloses a mind, so the word stretches from ground to attention.
senses.whyCN: 围住一片地方的区也能围住一个人的心思，于是这个词从地面伸到注意力。

intro.en: Zone comes from Latin zona and Greek zōnē, which both meant a belt worn round the body.
intro.cn: zone 出自拉丁语 zona 与希腊语 zōnē，两者都指缠在身上的腰带。

items.en: zōnē was the word for a belt or girdle, from a verb meaning to gird up.
items.cn: 希腊语 zōnē 指腰带、束带，出自意为「束起」的动词。

items.en: Latin zona kept the meaning of a belt and was also used for a band of the heavens.
items.cn: 拉丁语 zona 保留腰带之义，也用来指天上的一条带。

items.en: Writers used zonae for the belts of climate that circle the earth.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语作者用 zonae 指环抱地球的气候带。

items.en: The word entered English through French, where it meant both a band and a strip of land.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，法语中既指带子也指一条地。

items.en: English applied zone to areas of special rule, then to time zones and to states of mind.
items.cn: 英语把 zone 用到有特殊规则的区域，后用于时区与心理状态。

note.en: Zone is compared with its family and with other words for marked areas.
note.cn: zone 与自己的词族以及其它表示划定区域的词作对照。

entries.definition: the dividing of land into zones
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，区划，区域规划

entries.definition: divided into zones
entries.definitionCN: 同根形式，被划成区的

entries.definition: the quality of a sound, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，音调，词源不同

entries.definition: a part of a place with no fixed border
entries.definitionCN: 近义，一片区域，边界不固定

entries.definition: a large part of a country or the world
entries.definitionCN: 近义，较大的地区

entries.definition: a long band of land or climate
entries.definitionCN: 近义，成带的地域，也与词源相关

normalIntro.en: The image of a belt wrapped round the earth explains most of the word's senses.
normalIntro.cn: 一条缠在地球上的带子，解释了这个词的大多数义项。

normal.en: Time zones are belts wrapped round the globe, each one an hour apart.
normal.cn: 时区就是缠在地球上的带子，每条相隔一小时。

normal.en: Zoning is the act of drawing those belts on the map for planning.
normal.cn: zoning 就是在图上为规划画出这些带子。

normal.en: Greek zōnē meant a girdle, and the verb zōnnynai meant to gird up a garment.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zōnē 意为束带，动词 zōnnynai 意为束起衣服。

normal.en: The verb and the noun share a spelling, so land can be zoned into zones.
normal.cn: 动词与名词拼写相同，所以地可以被划成若干 zone。

normal.en: In the zone means absorbed in the work, while zone out means the opposite.
normal.cn: in the zone 指全神贯注，zone out 则相反。

abstract.en: Picture a waist band tightened around the middle of a body, and then around a whole planet.
abstract.cn: 想象一条腰带先系在腰上，然后系住整个星球。

abstract.en: Picture a dashed line on a car park floor, and everything inside it obeys one rule.
abstract.cn: 想象停车场地上一条虚线，线内一切都守同一条规矩。

abstract.en: Picture a radio dial with bands marked out, each playing something different.
abstract.cn: 想象一个刻着分格的收音机旋钮，每一格放不同的内容。

examples.en: Cars are not allowed in the school zone during the morning hours.
examples.cn: 上午时段校区内不许车辆通行。

examples.en: The earth is divided into twenty-four time zones.
examples.cn: 地球被划分为二十四个时区。

examples.en: The council zoned the land for housing twenty years ago.
examples.cn: 议会在二十年前就把这片地划作住宅区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「宗」——老家按宗族分片而居，一宗一片，界线清清楚楚，这种划出来的一片就是 zone。

root: 经由拉丁语 zona 借自希腊语 zōnē（腰带、束带），词根意为「束起」；后由腰带之义扩展为地球上的气候带与时区。

sensesIntro.en: A belt round the body becomes a belt round the earth, then an area with its own rules, an act of dividing land, and finally a state of attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条系在身上的带子先变成环抱地球的带，再变成有自己规则的区域、划分土地的动作，最后成了注意力的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dashed circle drawn on a map
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上画起的一块虚线圆圈

branches.en: The marked area keeps the picture of a band around something.
branches.cn: 划出的区域保留了「围住某物的一条带」这一画面。

branches.en: The earth's belts give climate and time zones.
branches.cn: 地球上的带子给出气候带与时区。

branches.en: Rules attached to a strip of land turn it into an official zone.
branches.cn: 给一条地附上规则，它就变成正式的区域。

branches.en: Drawing the belts becomes an action, so the noun works as a verb.
branches.cn: 画出这些带子成了动作，于是名词也能作动词。

branches.en: A zone around a mind names deep attention or its loss.
branches.cn: 围着心思的区，指专注或走神。

intro.en: Zone takes -ing and -ed, and appears in compounds such as time zone and school zone.
intro.cn: zone 能加 -ing、-ed，也出现在 time zone、school zone 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin zona is a straight borrowing from Greek, and the same root gives English the word girdle through a different path.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 zona 直接借自希腊语，同一词根经另一条路径给出英语的 girdle 一词。

items.exampleCN: 分区规划规则限制建筑高度。

items.example: The land is zoned for farming.

items.meaning: a belt of the earth with one clock time
items.meaningCN: 使用同一钟时的一片地域
items.example: The country spans three time zones.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家跨越三个时区。

items.meaning: an area with speed limits near a school
items.example: Slow down in the school zone.
Greek zōnē is the source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 zōnē 是这个词的来源。

items.example: Latin zona also names a band of the sky.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 zona 也指天上的一条带。

items.meaning: a belt worn round the waist
items.example: Girdle reached English by another route.
items.exampleCN: girdle 经另一条路径进入英语。

definition_zh: 调查；侦查；研究
definition_en: a careful, formal attempt to find out the facts about an event, problem, or claim
core_image: 手电照着地面，一步步顺着脚印往里查
scene: 办公室里文件摊满桌面，两个人对着账本逐页核对日期。 The investigation found that two payments had been recorded twice.
sceneCN: 这里 investigation 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为弄清事实而做的正式查证），句意为调查发现有两笔付款被记了两次。画面里的物件：账本、桌面、荧光笔。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 换 -ate，义为「调查；侦查」
由 investigate 加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由 investigate 词干加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」

senses.title: Official fact-finding
senses.definition: a formal process in which an authority examines evidence to establish the truth
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构审查证据、确定真相的正式过程
senses.example: A government investigation cleared the factory of any fault.
senses.exampleCN: 政府调查澄清这家工厂没有过错。
senses.why: Latin investigare meant "to follow the footprints", from in- plus vestigium, "track".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investigare 意为「跟着脚印走」，由 in- 加 vestigium「足迹」构成。

senses.title: Police or detective work
senses.definition: the work of police or detectives gathering facts about a suspected crime
senses.definitionCN: 警方或侦探就疑似犯罪收集事实的工作
senses.example: The investigation into the missing paintings lasted four years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失踪画作的侦查持续了四年。
senses.why: The footprint image fits best here: a detective literally follows a trail.
senses.whyCN: 「脚印」这个意象在这里最贴切：侦探就是顺着痕迹走的人。

senses.title: Careful study of a problem
senses.definition: a thorough academic or scientific study of a question
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题所作的详尽学术或科学研究
senses.example: Her investigation of soil bacteria changed the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她对土壤细菌的研究改变了这个领域。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word because a good study also follows traces until a pattern shows.
senses.whyCN: 科学借用了这个词，因为好的研究同样顺着痕迹走到规律显现。

intro.en: Investigation carries a picture of footprints: Latin vestigium means "track".
intro.cn: investigation 带着脚印的画面：拉丁语 vestigium 意为「足迹」。

items.en: vestigium meant "footprint, trace".
items.cn: vestigium 意为「脚印、痕迹」。

items.en: investigare meant "to follow a track".
items.cn: investigare 意为「跟着足迹走」。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the search itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这场追寻。

items.en: English took the noun for legal and official enquiries.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词用于法律与官方查问。

items.en: Science adopted it for systematic study as well.
items.cn: 科学界也采用它表示系统性研究。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vestigi- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for searching out facts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vestigi- 词干；近义组收表示查明事实的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to look into a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，同词干。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: A request to come somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请」，尾音相近。

entries.definition: A question or a formal look into facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「询问；查问」。

entries.definition: A close and often official examination.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「探查」，常指官方深入检查。

entries.definition: Systematic study to discover new facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究」，偏学术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all walk along a set of footprints.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都沿着同一串脚印走。

normal.en: in- means into, and vestigium means footprint.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vestigium 是「脚印」。

normal.en: To investigate is to follow the prints in.
normal.cn: investigate 就是顺着脚印往里查。

normal.en: The noun investigation is the whole walk.
normal.cn: 名词 investigation 指这整段路。

normal.en: An investigator is the one holding the torch.
normal.cn: investigator 是那个举着手电的人。

normal.en: Under investigation means the trail is still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是痕迹还热着。

abstract.en: Investigation is doubt that refuses to stay lazy.
abstract.cn: 调查是不肯偷懒的怀疑。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a footprint; the word is the act of bending down.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都留下脚印；这个词就是弯腰去看。

abstract.en: A careful inquiry turns noise into a line.
abstract.cn: 仔细的查证把杂音拉成一条线。

examples.en: The investigation into the fire took almost a year.
examples.cn: 对那场火灾的调查花了将近一年。

examples.en: Two officers were suspended while under investigation.
examples.cn: 两名警员在接受调查期间被停职。

examples.en: Her investigation of the lake water found traces of lead.
examples.cn: 她对湖水的调查发现了微量的铅。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestig（脚印）+ ation（名词）——顺着脚印查到底

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestigium「足迹」→ investigare「跟踪追查」→ investigatio → 英语 investigation。同族有 investigate、investigator、investigative。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an official inquiry, police detective work, and a thorough study of a question.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：官方查证、警方侦查，以及对某个问题的深入研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: following a trail of footprints until the truth shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：顺着脚印走，直到真相显现。

branches.en: THE FILE: officials checking records against facts.
branches.cn: 档案这条线：官员把记录与事实对照。

branches.en: THE TRAIL: detectives walking a case to its end.
branches.cn: 痕迹这条线：侦探把一个案子走到底。

branches.en: THE LAB: researchers chasing a pattern through data.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：研究者在数据里追一个规律。

branches.en: THE PROOF: both senses need evidence that holds up.
branches.cn: 证据这条线：两个义项都要站得住的证据。

branches.en: THE METHOD: both senses proceed step by step.
branches.cn: 方法这条线：两个义项都一步一步推进。

intro.en: Investigation is in- "into", vestigium "track", -ate the verb ending, and -ion for the act.
intro.cn: investigation 由 in-「进入」、vestigium「足迹」、动词尾 -ate 与名词尾 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium and investigare are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium 与 investigare 均有记载。

items.example: It marks walking inward along a trace.
The root is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是这个词的心脏。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The bare root still names a trace left behind.
items.exampleCN: 光词根仍指留下的痕迹。

definition_zh: 床单；薄片；一张；覆盖
definition_en: a large cloth for a bed, a thin flat piece of material, a single piece of paper, or to cover something
core_image: 一张床单被风鼓起，像一面柔软的帆
scene: 她换了床单。 She changed the sheets.
sceneCN: 这里 sheet 是「床单」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她换了床单。

senses.title: Bed cloth
senses.definition: a large cloth used on a bed
senses.definitionCN: 铺在床上的一大块布
senses.example: She changed the sheets.
senses.exampleCN: 她换了床单。
senses.why: This is the most familiar household sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最熟悉的家庭义项。

senses.title: Thin flat piece
senses.definition: a wide thin piece of material
senses.definitionCN: 一片宽而薄的材料
senses.example: The roof is covered with metal sheets.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶盖着金属板。
senses.why: A sheet is flat and wide like cloth.
senses.whyCN: 薄板像布一样平而宽。

senses.title: Piece of paper
senses.definition: a single piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 单独的一张纸
senses.example: Write your name on the sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的名字写在纸上。
senses.why: Paper is counted in sheets.
senses.whyCN: 纸张以张为单位计数。

senses.title: To cover
senses.definition: to cover something with a sheet or layer
senses.definitionCN: 用布或层状物覆盖某物
senses.example: Rain sheeted across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水成片扫过田野。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of spreading over.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为铺展覆盖的动词。

intro.en: Sheet comes from Old English sceata, a corner or piece of cloth.
intro.cn: sheet 源自古英语 sceata，意为布的一角或一块。

items.en: The root named a piece of cloth.
items.cn: 这个词根指一块布。

items.en: Sceata meant a corner or sheet of cloth.
items.cn: sceata 意为布角或布片。

items.en: Sheet named a large bed cloth.
items.cn: sheet 指大块床布。

items.en: Sheet named any broad thin surface.
items.cn: sheet 指任何宽薄的表面。

items.en: Paper and ice were counted in sheets.
items.cn: 纸张和冰层以 sheet 计量。

note.en: Sheet is compared with similar-looking words and with words for layers and cloth.
note.cn: 把 sheet 与形近词以及表示层和布的词作比较。

entries.definition: a farm animal with wool
entries.definitionCN: 绵羊

entries.definition: a flat board for storage
entries.definitionCN: 架子

entries.definition: to move something
entries.definitionCN: 移动

entries.definition: a flat piece over a surface
entries.definitionCN: 层

entries.definition: a flat board in a frame
entries.definitionCN: 面板

entries.definition: woven material
entries.definitionCN: 布

normalIntro.en: A sheet is one wide flat piece: cloth for a bed, paper for writing, metal for a roof.
normalIntro.cn: sheet 是一大片平坦之物：铺床的布、写字的纸、盖屋顶的金属板。

normal.en: The sheets are clean.
normal.cn: 床单很干净。

normal.en: Take a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: 拿一张纸。

normal.en: The ice sheet is melting.
normal.cn: 冰盖正在融化。

normal.en: He read the sheet music.
normal.cn: 他看着乐谱。

normal.en: Rain sheeted down the window.
normal.cn: 雨水成片顺着窗户流下。

abstract.en: A sheet is a surface that has given up depth.
abstract.cn: 薄片是放弃了深度的表面。

abstract.en: One sheet of paper can hold a whole argument.
abstract.cn: 一张纸可以承载整套论证。

abstract.en: Cloth and metal obey the same flat shape.
abstract.cn: 布与金属遵循同样的平坦形状。

examples.en: She changed the sheets.
examples.cn: 她换了床单。

examples.en: The roof is covered with metal sheets.
examples.cn: 屋顶盖着金属板。

examples.en: Write your name on the sheet.
examples.cn: 把你的名字写在纸上。

dict_mnemonic.text: sheet 源自古英语 sceata（布片），核心义「宽而薄的一片」，由床单推及纸张、金属板与冰盖。

root: 源自古英语 sceata（布的一角、一片），核心义「宽薄的平面物」。

sensesIntro.en: Sheet means a bed cloth, a thin flat piece, a piece of paper, or to cover.
sensesIntro.cn: sheet 意为床单、薄片、一张纸或覆盖。

core.en: One broad, flat piece of something.
core.cn: 某物宽而平的一片。

branches.en: Cloth spread on a bed.
branches.cn: 铺在床上的布。

branches.en: A wide thin panel of material.
branches.cn: 宽薄的板材。

branches.en: One piece of paper.
branches.cn: 一张纸。

branches.en: A layer spreading over a surface.
branches.cn: 铺展在表面的层。

branches.en: Cloth and paper are both counted in sheets.
branches.cn: 布与纸都以张计数。

intro.en: Sheet builds words for coverings, paper, and flat materials.
intro.cn: sheet 构成表示覆盖物、纸张和平材料的词。

latinIntro.en: Sheet has no Latin ancestor; Latin scheda, a sheet of paper, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sheet 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 scheda（纸页）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The rock has a sheetlike structure.

items.exampleCN: 这个箱子是金属薄板做的。

definition_zh: 种类；分类；整理
definition_en: a kind or type, to arrange things by type, or to deal with a problem
core_image: 桌上堆着混在一起的衣服，被按颜色分成几摞
scene: 请把衣服按颜色分类。 Please sort the clothes by colour.
sceneCN: 这里 sort 是「分类」（第 2 个义项）；句意：请把衣服按颜色分类。

senses.title: A kind or type
senses.definition: a group of people or things with shared qualities
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同特点的一类人或事物
senses.example: What sort of music do you like?
senses.exampleCN: 你喜欢哪种音乐？
senses.why: The oldest sense is the share or lot that decides a class.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是决定类别的份额或抽签结果。

senses.title: To arrange by type
senses.definition: to put things into groups by their type
senses.definitionCN: 按类型把事物分成组
senses.example: Please sort the clothes by colour.
senses.exampleCN: 请把衣服按颜色分类。
senses.why: From naming a class the word came to the act of making classes.
senses.whyCN: 从命名一个类别，这个词转而表示划分类别的动作。

senses.title: To deal with or tidy
senses.definition: to tidy something or solve a problem
senses.definitionCN: 把事物整理好或把问题处理好
senses.example: We must sort out this problem.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须解决这个问题。
senses.why: Sorting out puts a mess into order, so it also means solving.
senses.whyCN: sort out 把混乱理出头绪，因此也表示解决问题。

intro.en: Sort began as the drawing of lots and ended as the arranging of things.
intro.cn: sort 起初指抽签，最终表示对事物进行分类整理。

items.en: Sors, sortis meant a lot or a fate drawn by chance.
items.cn: sors（属格 sortis）意为抽签或凭运气得到的命运。

items.en: Sorte came to mean a kind or class.
items.cn: sorte 开始表示种类或类别。

items.en: Sort named a group of things of one kind.
items.cn: sort 指同一类的一组事物。

items.en: The verb appeared, meaning to arrange by kind.
items.cn: 动词形式出现，表示按类别整理。

items.en: The phrase sort out added the sense of solving.
items.cn: 短语 sort out 增加了「解决」的含义。

note.en: Sort is compared with look-alike words and words for kinds.
note.cn: 把 sort 与形近词以及表示种类的词作比较。

entries.definition: having a sharp taste
entries.definitionCN: 酸的

entries.definition: a game or physical activity
entries.definitionCN: 运动

entries.definition: black powder from smoke
entries.definitionCN: 煤烟

entries.definition: a type of thing
entries.definitionCN: 种类

entries.definition: a class with shared features
entries.definitionCN: 类型

entries.definition: a group of similar things
entries.definitionCN: 类别

normalIntro.en: Sort moves things from a mixed pile into clear groups.
normalIntro.cn: sort 把事物从混杂的一堆移入清晰的几组。

normal.en: What sort of music do you like?
normal.cn: 你喜欢哪种音乐？

normal.en: Please sort the clothes by colour.
normal.cn: 请把衣服按颜色分类。

normal.en: We must sort out this problem.
normal.cn: 我们必须解决这个问题。

normal.en: She sorted through the old letters.
normal.cn: 她翻检那些旧信件。

normal.en: It is a sort of quiet courage.
normal.cn: 那是一种安静的勇气。

abstract.en: Sort is the hand that gives a crowd its order.
abstract.cn: sort 是给杂乱之物赋予秩序的那只手。

abstract.en: Every sort begins with the courage to compare.
abstract.cn: 每一次分类都始于比较的勇气。

abstract.en: A sorted shelf is a quiet mind made visible.
abstract.cn: 整理好的书架，是看得见的平静心绪。

examples.en: What sort of music do you like?
examples.cn: 你喜欢哪种音乐？

examples.en: Please sort the clothes by colour.
examples.cn: 请把衣服按颜色分类。

examples.en: We must sort out this problem.
examples.cn: 我们必须解决这个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: sort 与 assort（分类、相配）、assortment（什锦）同族；sort of 是「有点」，sort out 是「整理、解决」，sort through 是「翻找」。

root: 来自拉丁语 sors（抽签、命运），经古法语 sorte（种类）进入英语，核心义从「抽签分份」转为「种类」与「分类」。

sensesIntro.en: Sort names a kind, the act of grouping by kind, and the tidying of a problem.
sensesIntro.cn: sort 指种类、按种类分组的动作，以及把问题整理解决。

core.en: To place like things together.
core.cn: 把同类的事物放在一起。

branches.en: A shelf holds books of every kind.
branches.cn: 书架上放着各种各样的书。

branches.en: Two piles of clothes grow on the table.
branches.cn: 桌上长出两摞衣服。

branches.en: A tangled drawer is emptied and rebuilt.
branches.cn: 乱糟糟的抽屉被清空又重新整理。

branches.en: Naming a kind and making kinds are twin acts.
branches.cn: 命名种类与划分种类是一对孪生动作。

branches.en: Arranging and solving both begin with sorting out.
branches.cn: 整理与解决，都从 sort out 开始。

intro.en: Sort builds verbs, nouns, and adjectives from one short stem.
intro.cn: sort 由一个短词干构成动词、名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is sors, sortis, a lot or fate.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 sors（属格 sortis），意为抽签或命运。

items.example: What sort of book is it?
These sorts of problems are common.
Sorting the files took an hour.
The sorter handles hundreds of letters.
items.exampleCN: 分拣机每小时处理数百封信。

items.example: The shop assorts its goods by colour.
items.exampleCN: 这家店按颜色分类摆放商品。

items.example: She bought a box of assorted sweets.
The stall sold an assortment of fruit.
items.exampleCN: 摊位上卖着各式各样的水果。

latinEntries.example: Sors gave each man his share.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 抽签分给每个人应得的一份。

definition_zh: 名声；声誉；名望
definition_en: the opinion that people have about someone or something, based on past behaviour or quality
core_image: 街坊邻居提起这个名字时形成的共同评价，像一块慢慢磨亮的招牌
scene: 这家小面馆从不打广告，靠街坊口口相传，几十年攒下了好名声。 The little restaurant earned its reputation one bowl at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 reputation 是「名声；声誉」（第 1 个义项：人们根据过往表现形成的评价）；句意：这家小馆一碗一碗地赢得好名声。

senses.title: The opinion people have
senses.definition: the general opinion that people have about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人们普遍持有的对某人或某物的看法
senses.example: The school has a reputation for strict teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以教学严格著称。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to think over, so a reputation is the opinion formed after repeated consideration.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「反复思量」，所以名声是经过反复考虑后形成的看法。

senses.title: A good name
senses.definition: the respect and trust that come from being known to behave well
senses.definitionCN: 因表现良好而获得的尊重与信任
senses.example: He built his reputation on honest dealing.
senses.exampleCN: 他以诚信经营建立了声誉。
senses.why: Because people want a good opinion rather than a bad one, the word often carries the positive sense of a good name.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们想要好评价而不是坏评价，这个词常带有「好名声」的正面含义。

senses.title: The state of being known
senses.definition: the state of being well known by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被许多人熟知的状态
senses.example: Her reputation spread far beyond the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她的名声传到了城市之外很远的地方。
senses.why: A widely shared opinion naturally becomes fame, so being known is a further extension of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 被广泛共享的看法自然成为名望，所以「被熟知」是同一想法的进一步延伸。

intro.en: Reputation comes from Latin reputatio, from reputare, to think over, built from re- and putare, to consider.
intro.cn: reputation 来自拉丁语 reputatio，源自动词 reputare（反复思量），由 re- 与 putare（思考、估算）构成。

items.en: Putare means to think, reckon, or judge, and it also gives us compute.
items.cn: putare 意为思考、估算或判断，也是 compute 的来源。

items.en: Reputare adds re-, over again, and means to consider something repeatedly.
items.cn: reputare 加上 re-（反复），意为反复考虑某事。

items.en: Reputatio names the judging and the standing that results from it.
items.cn: reputatio 指评判行为以及由此形成的地位。

items.en: Old French reputation keeps the sense of public estimation.
items.cn: 古法语 reputation 保留「公众评价」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reputation names what people generally think of a person.
items.cn: 中古英语 reputation 指人们对某人的普遍看法。

items.en: Modern English uses it for both good standing and simple fame.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它既指良好声誉，也指单纯的知名度。

note.en: Reputation belongs to a Latin thinking-and-judging family, and it sits close to words for fame and standing.
note.cn: reputation 属于拉丁语「思考与评判」词族，与名望和地位的词相邻。

entries.definition: the opinion generally held about someone
entries.definitionCN: 名声；声望

entries.definition: having a good reputation
entries.definitionCN: 声誉好的

entries.definition: believed by many people to be something
entries.definitionCN: 据称的；号称的

entries.definition: the state of being known by many people
entries.definitionCN: 名声；名气

entries.definition: the reputation a person or company has
entries.definitionCN: 名声；名誉

entries.definition: a person's rank or status in a group
entries.definitionCN: 地位；声望

entries.definition: respect gained through success or importance
entries.definitionCN: 威望；声望

normalIntro.en: Reputation contains repute, from Latin putare, to think, so the word is literally what people have thought about you over and over.
normalIntro.cn: reputation 含有 repute，源自拉丁语 putare（思考），所以这个词字面上就是「人们反复思量后对你的看法」。

normal.en: Re- means again, and putare means think: think about someone again and again, and a reputation forms.
normal.cn: re- 表示反复，putare 表示思考：反复想一个人，就形成名声。

normal.en: Have a reputation for is the pattern that follows the word most often.
normal.cn: have a reputation for 是这个词最常见的搭配模式。

normal.en: Build a reputation suggests it takes time and repeated acts.
normal.cn: build a reputation 暗示名声需要时间和反复行动。

normal.en: Damage a reputation is much faster than building one.
normal.cn: damage a reputation 比建立名声快得多。

normal.en: Compare reputable: the adjective means having a good reputation.
normal.cn: 对比 reputable：形容词意为「有好名声的」。

abstract.en: Picture a shop sign polished brighter by every satisfied customer.
abstract.cn: 想象每位满意的顾客都把店招擦得更亮一点。

abstract.en: Imagine neighbours repeating the same story about a person until it sticks.
abstract.cn: 想象邻居反复讲同一个人的故事，直到它固定下来。

abstract.en: Think of a name written in many notebooks across a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写进全城许多本笔记本。

examples.en: The company has a reputation for paying on time.
examples.cn: 这家公司以按时付款著称。

examples.en: One scandal can ruin a lifetime's reputation.
examples.cn: 一场丑闻可能毁掉一生的声誉。

examples.en: She arrived with a reputation as a tough negotiator.
examples.cn: 她来时已以强硬谈判者闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（反复）+ put（思考）＝人们反复思量后形成的看法，即名声；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（反复）+ putare（思考、判断）→ reputare（反复思量）→ reputatio（评价、声望）→ 古法语 reputation → 中古英语 reputation。

sensesIntro.en: An opinion formed by repeated thought comes first, then the good version people want, and finally the wide fame that spreads it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有反复思考形成的评价，再是人们想要的正面版本，最后是把它传播开来的广泛名望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name polished by what people repeatedly say and think about it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被人们反复谈论和思量，渐渐磨亮。

branches.en: The general opinion is the neutral core sense.
branches.cn: 普遍看法，是中性的核心义项。

branches.en: The opinion becomes a good name when it is positive.
branches.cn: 当评价是正面的，就成为好名声。

branches.en: A widely held opinion spreads into fame and public recognition.
branches.cn: 被广泛持有的看法扩散为名望与公众认可。

branches.en: Neutral opinion and good name differ only in direction.
branches.cn: 中性评价与好名声只在方向上不同。

branches.en: Good standing and wide fame both grow from what others say.
branches.cn: 良好声誉与广泛名望都从他人的言谈中生长出来。

intro.en: Reputation is a Latin noun formed on reputare, with English relatives built from the repute stem.
intro.cn: reputation 是在拉丁动词 reputare 基础上构成的名词，其英语亲属词由 repute 词干派生。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means over again, and putare means to think or judge, so reputare is to think something over.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示反复，putare 表示思考或判断，所以 reputare 就是「反复思量」。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 reputare 与 reputation 开头。

items.example: Putare is the root of reputation and compute.
items.exampleCN: putare 是 reputation 与 compute 的词根。
reputare 由 re- 与 putare 合成。

items.example: Reputatio is the Latin noun behind reputation.
items.exampleCN: reputatio 是 reputation 背后的拉丁名词。

items.example: Reputation keeps the Latin noun shape.
items.exampleCN: reputation 保留了拉丁名词形态。

items.example: Reputable adds -able to the repute stem.
items.exampleCN: reputable 在 repute 词干后加 -able。

items.example: Reputed adds -ed to the repute stem.
items.exampleCN: reputed 在 repute 词干后加 -ed。

definition_zh: 雇主；用人单位
definition_en: a person or organization that pays others to work
core_image: 办公室里的经理，负责签下新员工的合同
scene: 她的雇主允许她在家工作。 Her employer allows her to work from home.
sceneCN: 这里 employer 是「雇主」（第 1 个义项：付钱雇用别人的人或机构）；句意：她的雇主允许她在家工作。

senses.title: A person who hires workers
senses.definition: a person who pays one or more people to work for them
senses.definitionCN: 付钱请一个或多个人为自己工作的人
senses.example: Her employer gave her a raise.
senses.exampleCN: 她的雇主给她加了薪。
senses.why: The ending -er marks the doer, so the employer is the one who performs the hiring.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 标记执行者，因此 employer 是实施雇用的一方。

senses.title: An organization that provides jobs
senses.definition: a company or institution that provides paid work to many people
senses.definitionCN: 为许多人提供有薪工作的公司或机构
senses.example: The hospital is the largest employer in town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院是镇上最大的用人单位。
senses.why: Hiring is done by institutions as well as individuals, so the word extends to organizations.
senses.whyCN: 雇用不仅由个人完成，也由机构完成，因此这个词扩展到组织。

intro.en: Employer adds the doer ending -er to employ, naming the side that hires.
intro.cn: employer 在 employ 后加法语执行者词尾 -er，命名雇用的一方。

items.en: Employer is both a verb and a noun for one who uses or engages.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 既是动词，也指使用或聘用的人。

items.en: English borrows the verb employ and builds the noun with -er.
items.cn: 英语借入动词 employ，并用 -er 构成名词。

items.en: Employer settles as the party that pays for work.
items.cn: 在近代早期，employer 固定为支付劳动报酬的一方。

items.en: Factories make employer a common word in law and trade.
items.cn: 工业时代让 employer 成为法律与商业中的常用词。

items.en: Employer now includes companies and public institutions.
items.cn: 现代英语中，employer 包括公司和公共机构。

note.en: The employer pays; the employee is paid; the boss manages, and the company provides jobs.
note.cn: employer 付钱，employee 领钱，boss 管理，company 提供岗位。

root: employ 加法语来源的执行者词尾 -er。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the person who hires and also the organization that provides jobs.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指雇用他人的个人，也指提供岗位的组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand offering a signed contract.
core.cn: 核心意象：递出已签合同的手。

branches.en: The base sense is the person who hires.
branches.cn: 基本义是雇用他人的个人。

branches.en: The same role belongs to companies and institutions.
branches.cn: 同样的角色也属于公司和机构。

branches.en: Both sides pay for work and sign agreements.
branches.cn: 两者都为劳动付钱并签署协议。

branches.en: The -er ending marks the active side.
branches.cn: 词尾 -er 标记主动的一方。

branches.en: A large employer shapes a whole town's jobs.
branches.cn: 大型雇主塑造整个城镇的就业。

intro.en: Employer is employ plus -er, the ending for the person who performs an action.
intro.cn: employer 是 employ 加 -er，即表示动作执行者的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root plic-, to fold, underlies the whole employ family.
latinIntro.cn: 意为折叠的拉丁词根 plic- 支撑整个 employ 词族。

items.example: Employ is the base of employer.

items.example: A contract joins employer and employee.
The staff depends on the employer.

definition_zh: 挣扎；奋斗；艰难
definition_en: to fight hard against difficulty, or a hard fight or effort
core_image: 一个人在水里拼命划动双臂，向岸边靠近
scene: 他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。 He struggled through the water toward the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 struggle 是「挣扎」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。

senses.title: Fight against difficulty
senses.definition: to use great effort against something difficult or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 为对抗困难或危险而拼尽全力
senses.example: He struggled through the water toward the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。
senses.why: This is effort against a force.
senses.whyCN: 这是与一股力量对抗所花的力气。

senses.title: A hard fight
senses.definition: a difficult fight or a long effort
senses.definitionCN: 艰难的斗争或长期的努力
senses.example: Losing the job was a real struggle for her.
senses.exampleCN: 失去工作对她来说是一段真正的艰难。
senses.why: The verb becomes the thing endured.
senses.whyCN: 动词在这里变成了所承受的事情。

senses.title: Have trouble doing
senses.definition: to find something very difficult to do
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某事非常难做
senses.example: He struggles with math.
senses.exampleCN: 他学数学很吃力。
senses.why: The fight is now with a task.
senses.whyCN: 这时的对手变成了一项任务。

intro.en: Struggle comes from Middle English strogelen, to fight hard.
intro.cn: struggle 来自中古英语 strogelen，意为奋力搏斗。

items.en: The word's exact source is not certain.
items.cn: 这个词的确切来源并不确定。

items.en: Strogelen meant to fight or strive.
items.cn: strogelen 意为搏斗或奋力。

items.en: Struggle described effort against danger.
items.cn: struggle 描写与危险对抗的努力。

items.en: It also named a long hard effort.
items.cn: 它也指长期艰苦的努力。

items.en: Struggle with came to mean having trouble.
items.cn: struggle with 引申为做某事很吃力。

note.en: Struggle is compared with look-alike words and with words for fighting hard.
note.cn: 把 struggle 与形近词以及表示奋力抗争的词作比较。

entries.definition: the way parts are joined
entries.definitionCN: 结构

entries.definition: having great power
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的

entries.definition: demanding obedience
entries.definitionCN: 严格的

entries.definition: to use force against someone
entries.definitionCN: 战斗

entries.definition: to try very hard
entries.definitionCN: 努力奋斗

entries.definition: to fight a long hard fight
entries.definitionCN: 苦战

normalIntro.en: Struggle is effort that meets resistance and keeps going.
normalIntro.cn: struggle 是遇上阻力却仍继续的用力。

normal.en: She struggled to open the door.
normal.cn: 她费力地想把门打开。

normal.en: Many families struggle with high rents.
normal.cn: 许多家庭在高房租下艰难生活。

normal.en: They struggled against the strong wind.
normal.cn: 他们与强风搏斗。

normal.en: It was a long struggle for equality.
normal.cn: 那是为平等进行的长期斗争。

normal.en: He struggles with the new language.
normal.cn: 他学这门新语言很吃力。

abstract.en: A struggle is a door that does not open by itself.
abstract.cn: 挣扎，是一扇不会自己打开的门。

abstract.en: What resists you also teaches you.
abstract.cn: 让你受阻的东西，也在教你。

abstract.en: Small daily struggles build quiet strength.
abstract.cn: 每天的小挣扎，垒出安静的力量。

examples.en: He struggled through the water toward the shore.
examples.cn: 他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。

examples.en: Losing the job was a real struggle for her.
examples.cn: 失去工作对她来说是一段真正的艰难。

examples.en: He struggles with math.
examples.cn: 他学数学很吃力。

dict_mnemonic.text: struggle 的核心是「对抗着用力」；在水里对抗是挣扎，对命运长期用力是奋斗，面对难题吃力就是 struggle with。

root: 来自中古英语 strogelen（奋力搏斗），确切来源不确定；由身体上的挣扎，引申为长期的奋斗，再用于表示做某事很吃力。

sensesIntro.en: Struggle is effort against danger, a long hard fight, or trouble with a task.
sensesIntro.cn: struggle 是与危险对抗的力气、长期艰苦的斗争，或面对任务时的吃力。

core.en: Arms pushing against deep water.

branches.en: A swimmer fights the current.

branches.en: What is hard to learn is also worth learning.

每个奋斗者都需要希望。

definition_zh: 乳房；胸部；胸怀

definition_zh: 运动；移动；动作；社会运动；乐章；走势；调动；排便
definition_en: an act of changing position or place, or an organized group working for a shared aim, or a section of a musical work
core_image: 一队人举着同样的牌子从广场一端走到另一端，脚步连成一道推进的横线
scene: 广场上，人们举着同样的牌子从一端走向另一端，队伍越来越长，喊声连成一片。 The movement began with a few students and soon filled the square.
sceneCN: 这里 movement 指有共同诉求的群体性运动（第 3 个义项：社会运动）；句意：这场运动从几名学生开始，很快站满了广场。图中可辨识物件：手写标语牌、扩音器、横幅、统一的袖标；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 运动；移动；动作；社会运动；乐章；走势

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the act or process of changing position or place
senses.definitionCN: 改变位置或处所的动作或过程
senses.example: A slow movement of the shelf warned that the wall was settling.
senses.exampleCN: 架子缓缓移位，说明墙体在下沉。
senses.why: Movement is the native noun of the verb move, and its oldest sense is simply the fact of changing place.
senses.whyCN: movement 是动词 move 的本族名词，最古老的意思就是「换了地方」这件事。

senses.title: A single action of the body
senses.definition: one deliberate action or gesture, especially of the hand or body
senses.definitionCN: 一次有意的动作或姿态，尤指手或身体的
senses.example: With one movement she folded the letter and sealed it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个动作就把信折好封上了。
senses.why: A process can be cut into single acts, and one of those acts is also called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 一个过程可以切成一个个单独的动作，其中一次也叫 movement。

senses.title: An organized campaign for a cause
senses.titleCN: 为某一诉求组织起来的社会运动
senses.definition: a group of people acting together over time to bring about a change in society or policy
senses.definitionCN: 一群人长期共同行动，以求改变社会或政策
senses.example: The movement for clean rivers spread from one town to the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净河流的运动从一个镇扩展到整个河谷。
senses.why: In the nineteenth century people acting together were seen as one body on the move, so a campaign became a movement.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪，人们把共同行动的一群人看作一个在移动的整体，于是运动便成了一项社会运动。

senses.title: A section of a musical work
senses.titleCN: 长篇乐曲中的一个乐章
senses.definition: a self-contained part of a long musical composition, such as a symphony
senses.definitionCN: 长篇乐曲（如交响曲）中相对独立的一部分
senses.example: The second movement is slow and almost silent.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章缓慢而近乎无声。
senses.why: Music was thought of as advancing in stages; each stage is a movement within the whole work.
senses.whyCN: 人们把音乐想成一段段向前推进；每一个阶段就是整部作品里的一个乐章。

senses.title: A trend in figures or opinion
senses.definition: a change in level, price or opinion over time, seen as a direction
senses.definitionCN: 水平、价格或舆论随时间的变化，被看作一个方向
senses.example: The upward movement in rents began before the new bridge opened.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨走势在新桥通车前就开始了。
senses.why: A line on a chart that keeps going one way looks like something travelling, so a trend is called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 图表上一直朝一个方向走的线，看起来像有东西在行进，因此趋势也被称为 movement。

senses.title: The mechanism inside a clock
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts that drives a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 驱动钟表的整套运动部件
senses.example: The watch has a hand-wound movement and a glass back.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是手上链机芯，背面是玻璃的。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: A relocation of troops or supplies
senses.definition: the organized moving of troops, ships or supplies from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地把部队、船只或物资从一处移到另一处
senses.example: Satellite images tracked the movement of trucks along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像追踪了卡车沿边境的调动。
senses.why: A body of men or goods changing place is still the plain sense, made formal by military use.
senses.whyCN: 一批人或货物换地方，仍是那个直白的意思，只是被军事用法正式化了。

senses.title: A bowel movement
senses.definition: an act of emptying the bowels, used as a neutral medical term
senses.definitionCN: 排空肠道的一次动作，用作中性的医学说法
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's movements after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录了病人术后的排便情况。
senses.why: Medicine needed a plain, polite noun for a bodily action, and the ordinary word for moving served.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个平实而礼貌的词来指这一身体动作，于是用了「移动」这个普通词。

intro.en: Movement comes through Old French movement from movoir, the French form of Latin movere 'to move'. The musical and social senses are later growths from the plain idea of something advancing.
intro.cn: movement 经古法语 movement 来自 movoir，即拉丁 movere「移动」的法语形式。乐章义与社会运动义都是后来的引申，源自「某物在向前推进」这一朴素想法。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to set going, and it is the source of the whole French and English family.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动，是整个法语与英语词族的源头。

items.en: The French verb movoir or moveir meant to move and gave English the verb move.
items.cn: 法语动词 movoir 或 moveir 意为移动，并给英语带来了动词 move。

items.en: The noun movement named the act of moving; it uses the same action-noun ending as many French words in -ment.
items.cn: 名词 movement 指移动这一动作；它用的动作名词词尾，与许多以 -ment 结尾的法语词相同。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, at first for physical movement and later for a single action.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个名词，起初指物理移动，后来也指单次动作。

items.en: From the eighteenth century a movement named a section of a symphony or sonata, following the idea of music advancing by stages.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，movement 指交响曲或奏鸣曲中的一个部分，沿用「音乐分段推进」的想法。

items.en: The collective sense for a campaign is a nineteenth-century growth, when large groups acting for a cause were described as one moving body.
items.cn: 指社会运动的集体义是十九世纪长出的，当时为某一诉求行动的大群人是被当作一个移动的整体来描述。

note.en: The first group shares the verb move and is often mistaken for the noun; the second group separates movement from motion, campaign and trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享动词 move，常与这个名词混淆；第二组把 movement 与 motion、campaign、trend 等词区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a countable noun for one act of moving; movement is the noun of the process or the campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也可数名词指一次移动；movement 指过程或社会运动。

entries.definition: Move plus -able: able to be moved, said of furniture or a feast day; it is an adjective, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表「能够」的词尾构成：可被移动的，用于家具或不固定的节期；是形容词，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -ing: either in the act of moving or able to stir the feelings, as a moving speech does.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表进行或性质的词尾构成：或指正在移动，或指能打动人心，如感人的演讲。

entries.definition: A shortened form of moving picture, from the moving images on film; it is a thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 「活动影像」一词的缩略，来自胶片上移动的影像；指作品，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -er: a person or thing that moves something, or a company that transports goods.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表施动者的词尾构成：推动某事的人或物，也指搬家公司。

entries.definition: Often a single physical act or a formal proposal; movement is wider and covers campaigns and trends.
entries.definitionCN: 多指单次物理动作或正式动议；movement 范围更宽，还涵盖社会运动与趋势。

entries.definition: An organized series of actions for a goal; a movement is broader and longer, and usually social.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目标组织的一系列行动；movement 更宽、更久，通常带社会性。

entries.definition: A strong effort or campaign to reach a target, often official; it stresses the push, not the people.
entries.definitionCN: 为达目标的有力推动或活动，常是官方发起的；强调推动力，不强调人群。

entries.definition: The general direction in which something is changing; movement can name a change in figures but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 事物变化的总方向；movement 也能指数字变动，但更具体。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles; it is technical and not social.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，用于动物和交通工具；属技术用语，不含社会义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and movement is the noun made from the French verb.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，movement 是由法语动词变来的名词。

normal.en: The family runs move, movable, moving, movie, mover.
normal.cn: 同族词有 move、movable、moving、movie、mover。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: social movement, slow movement, upward movement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：社会运动、慢乐章、上升走势。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns an action into a noun, as in agreement and management.
normal.cn: 名词词尾把动作变成名词，如「同意」与「管理」二词。

normal.en: A clock's movement is the works that keep it moving, a trade term from watchmaking.
normal.cn: 钟表的 movement 是让它持续运转的机芯，这是制表业的行业说法。

abstract.en: Picture one person walking, then a hundred walking in the same direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走，然后一百个人朝同一个方向走。

abstract.en: Picture a symphony advancing one stage at a time, each stage its own room.
abstract.cn: 想象一部交响曲一段段向前走，每个阶段自成一间屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph climbing and someone calling that climb a movement.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上爬，有人把这段爬升叫 movement。

examples.en: The movement of goods across the border slowed after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，货物过境的流动变慢了。

examples.en: The civil rights movement changed the town's hiring rules.
examples.cn: 民权运动改变了这座小镇的用工规定。

examples.en: A thermostat senses the movement of air through the duct.
examples.cn: 恒温器感知空气在管道中的流动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「move（挪）+ ment（门特）」——挪一挪，人群就成了一场运动；movement 移动、运动、乐章

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ 古法语 movoir「移动」→ 古法语名词 movement「移动、动作」→ 英语 movement；乐章义由乐曲内部的推进，社会运动义为十九世纪集体行动的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one body in motion: it changes place, makes a single act, gathers into a campaign, advances as a section of music, climbs as a trend, drives a clock, moves as troops, and passes as a bodily function.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「在动的身体」展开：它换位、做出一次动作、聚成一场运动、作为乐曲的一部分推进、作为趋势上升、驱动机芯、作为部队调动，最后成为一种身体功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people walking together in one direction, their steps forming an advancing line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人朝同一方向走，脚步连成一条推进的横线。

chain: A LINE ON A CHART RISES

branches.en: PLAIN MOVING: one body changes place, and one deliberate action of the hand is carved out of it.
branches.cn: 直白的动：一具身体换了地方，其中切出手的一次有意动作。

branches.en: PEOPLE TOGETHER: many bodies moving for one cause become a social movement.
branches.cn: 众人同行：许多身体为一个诉求而动，聚成社会运动。

branches.en: A WORK IN STAGES: music advancing by sections gives the musical movement its name.
branches.cn: 分段推进的作品：音乐按段落向前，乐章由此得名。

branches.en: A CLIMB ON A CHART: the same advance is read as a trend in figures.
branches.cn: 图表上的爬升：同一种推进被读成数字的走势。

branches.en: MOVING PARTS AND BODIES: a watch's works, a column of trucks, and the bowels all carry the plain sense into new settings.
branches.cn: 运动部件与身体：钟表机芯、车队与肠道，都把直白义带进新的场合。

intro.en: Movement is a French action noun built on the Latin verb of moving, with the same ending that forms many English nouns.
intro.cn: movement 是一个由拉丁「移动」动词构成的法语动作名词，用的词尾也构成许多英语名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives move, motion, motive and motor; the French noun movement adds the action-noun ending to the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 move、motion、motive 与 motor；法语名词 movement 则在同一个动词上加动作名词词尾。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The French verb passed into English as move.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词进入英语后成为 move。

items.example: The machine's movements are smooth and silent.

items.meaning: to shift; to touch the feelings

definition_zh: 燃料；给……加燃料；助长
definition_en: a material that is burned for heat or power, or to give power to something
core_image: 汽车停在加油站，油枪正往里注油
scene: 这辆车的油箱快空了，得找地方加油。 The car is low on fuel and needs to stop.

senses.title: Material burned for power
senses.definition: a material such as wood, oil, or gas that is burned to produce heat or power
senses.definitionCN: 木柴、石油或天然气等燃烧后产生热或动力的材料
senses.example: The car is low on fuel and needs to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的油箱快空了，得找地方加油。
senses.why: This is the basic material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的材料义项。

senses.title: Give power to
senses.definition: to give fuel to an engine or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 为发动机或交通工具提供燃料
senses.example: The plane was fuelled before takeoff.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机起飞前加好了油。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of supplying.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示供给的动词。

senses.title: Make stronger

senses.exampleCN: 他的话只是让争论更激烈。
senses.why: Fuel feeds a fire, and also feeds conflict.

items.en: The verb came to mean stirring up feeling.

core.en: Material that feeds fire or motion.

branches.en: Words add heat to a quarrel.

branches.cn: 材料与加注动作彼此相属。
