definition_zh: 午夜；子夜；午夜十二点；深夜；午夜的
definition_en: twelve o'clock at night, the quiet hours around it, the deepest darkness of the night, or attributive use before another noun
core_image: 钟面两根指针叠在最高处，窗外一片深黑
scene: 最后一班车开走后，站台上只剩一盏灯，钟声刚敲过整点，整条街都沉进黑暗里。 The train left the station at midnight, and the platform fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里 midnight 是「午夜十二点」（第 1 个义项：一天结束、下一天开始的整点）；句意为列车在午夜离站，站台随之安静下来。画面里可抓住的物件：站台灯、末班车、钟面。

pos.zh: 午夜；子夜；午夜十二点；深夜

derivatives.zh: 由 midnight 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「午夜的、深夜般的」，属文学罕用说法
与 midnight 同用 mid- 前缀，指仲夏、夏至前后
与 midnight 同用 mid- 前缀，指仲冬、冬至前后

senses.title: Twelve o'clock at night
senses.definition: the exact moment when one day ends and the next begins
senses.definitionCN: 一天结束、下一天开始的那一刹那
senses.example: The clock struck midnight before anyone spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人开口，钟就敲响了午夜十二点。
senses.why: Old English midniht is mid plus niht, the middle of the night; it first marked the point halfway between sunset and sunrise, and the clock later fixed that middle at twelve.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 midniht 就是 mid 加 niht，即「夜的正中」；它最初标记的是日落到日出之间的中点，后来钟表把这个中点固定在十二点。

senses.title: The quiet hours around twelve
senses.definition: the hours on either side of twelve, when most people are asleep
senses.definitionCN: 十二点前后的一段时间，多数人已经入睡
senses.example: Guards change shifts around midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵在午夜前后换班。
senses.why: Once the word names the darkest point, it also covers the still hours that surround it, because sleep and silence gather on both sides of twelve.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指到夜的最深处，也就覆盖了围绕它的那几个寂静小时，因为睡眠与安静都在十二点两侧聚集。

senses.title: The deepest darkness of the night
senses.definition: the deep darkness of night, or a figurative moment of greatest gloom
senses.definitionCN: 夜的深沉黑暗，也比喻最阴沉、最低落的时刻
senses.example: The village lay in midnight darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 村子陷在深夜的黑暗里。
senses.why: Because midnight is the point farthest from daylight, writers use it for any moment of deepest darkness or despair, moving from clock time to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 因为午夜是离白昼最远的时刻，作家便用它指任何最黑暗、最绝望的关头，词义从钟点时间转向情绪。

senses.title: Happening at twelve at night
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that occurs or appears at midnight
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指在午夜发生或出现的事物
senses.example: They caught the midnight train to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搭上午夜的列车去海边。
senses.why: A time noun placed before another noun works like an adjective; midnight train and midnight snack simply shorten at midnight without changing the word's form.
senses.whyCN: 时间名词放在另一个名词前就像形容词；midnight train 与 midnight snack 只是把 at midnight 压缩，词形并未改变。

intro.en: Midnight is an old compound of the middle root and the word for night, and its meaning has moved from the midpoint of darkness to the fixed hour of the clock.
intro.cn: midnight 是「中间」词根与「夜」组成的古老复合词，含义已从黑暗的中点移到钟表上固定的整点。

items.en: The compound is reconstructed as *midjanahts, middle plus night, a label for the centre of the dark hours.
items.cn: 这个复合词一般重构为 *midjanahts，即「中间」加「夜」，用来标记黑暗时段的中心。

items.en: Old English midniht kept that shape and named the middle of the night rather than a point on any instrument.
items.cn: 古英语的 midniht 保留了这一结构，指夜的正中，而不是任何仪器上的刻度。

items.en: Middle English midnight stayed close to the older sense while clocks began to divide the night into equal hours.
items.cn: 中古英语的 midnight 仍贴近较早的含义，而与此同时钟表开始把夜晚划成等长的时辰。

items.en: Once mechanical clocks were common, midnight settled at twelve, the moment that separates one calendar day from the next.
items.cn: 机械钟普及之后，midnight 固定在十二点，成为把一个日历日与下一个分开的那一刻。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative sense of deepest gloom and the attributive use seen in midnight train and midnight snack.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「最深的阴郁」这一比喻义，以及 midnight train、midnight snack 中可见的定语用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built with the same mid or night material; the near-meaning group collects phrases for the dead of night.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 mid 或 night 材料构成的词；近义组收表示深夜的说法。

entries.definition: Happening or appearing at midnight; a rare, literary adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在午夜发生或出现的；罕用的文学形容词。

entries.definition: The middle of summer, around the longest day.
entries.definitionCN: 夏季的正中，约在白昼最长的那几天。

entries.definition: The middle of winter, around the shortest day.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季的正中，约在白昼最短的那几天。

entries.definition: The middle of the week, around Wednesday.
entries.definitionCN: 一周的中间，约在周三前后。

entries.definition: The late night hours when magic was once thought to be strongest.
entries.definitionCN: 深夜时分，旧时被认为魔法最强的时刻。

entries.definition: The darkest and quietest part of the night.
entries.definitionCN: 夜里最黑、最安静的时候。

entries.definition: The hours after midnight, usually between one and four.
entries.definitionCN: 午夜之后的凌晨时分，通常指一点到四点。

normalIntro.en: Midnight is mid plus night, and the family around it keeps joining the middle root to units of time or to the dark half of the day.
normalIntro.cn: midnight 就是 mid 加 night，它周围的一族词不断把「中间」词根接到时间单位或一天中黑暗的那一半上。

normal.en: Midnight is mid plus night, so the word literally says middle of the night.
normal.cn: midnight 就是 mid 加 night，字面说的就是「夜的正中」。

normal.en: Old English wrote it as one word, midniht, which is why the modern spelling has no hyphen or space.
normal.cn: 古英语就把它写成一个词 midniht，所以现代拼写既不加连字符也不留空格。

normal.en: The clock sense is younger than the word: midnight first meant the middle of the dark hours, not the number twelve.
normal.cn: 钟点义比这个词本身年轻：midnight 最初指黑暗时段的中点，而不是数字十二。

normal.en: Burn the midnight oil comes from lamps that burned oil, and it keeps the word tied to late work.
normal.cn: burn the midnight oil 来自点油灯的年代，这个说法把 midnight 牢牢系在深夜劳作上。

normal.en: Set it beside midday: the same middle, but on the dark side of the clock.
normal.cn: 把它和 midday 并排看：同样是「中间」，只是落在钟面偏暗的那一侧。

abstract.en: Two hands stacked at the top of the dial, and the street outside goes completely dark.
abstract.cn: 两根指针叠在表盘最高处，外面的街道彻底暗下来。

abstract.en: Midnight is the seam of the calendar: the old day ends and the new one begins in the same tick.
abstract.cn: midnight 是日历的接缝：旧的一天与新的一天在同一个滴答里交接。

abstract.en: The word moves from a point on a dial to a feeling of total gloom, because both sit as far as possible from daylight.
abstract.cn: 这个词从表盘上的一个点走到「彻底阴郁」的感受，因为两者都离白昼尽可能远。

examples.en: The clock struck midnight before anyone spoke.
examples.cn: 还没人开口，钟就敲响了午夜十二点。

examples.en: Guards change shifts around midnight.
examples.cn: 卫兵在午夜前后换班。

examples.en: They caught the midnight train to the coast.
examples.cn: 他们搭上午夜的列车去海边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密的」加「奈特」——夜密得看不见路，钟点又落到最低处；midnight 是午夜。

root: 古英语 midniht，由 midd（中间）与 niht（夜）复合，一般重构为原始日耳曼语 *midjanahts；拉丁语以 medius（中间）加 nox（夜）构成 media nox，思路相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the middle of the night; the senses run from the clock hour to the surrounding quiet hours, to figurative darkness, and to attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是夜的正中；各义项从钟表整点，扩到前后的寂静时段、比喻性的黑暗，以及作定语的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands stacked at the top of a clock dial while the street outside is completely dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟面两根指针叠在最高处，外面的街道一片漆黑。

branches.en: a clock striking while a platform empties
branches.cn: 站台空下去时钟声敲响

branches.en: guards trading places in the dark
branches.cn: 卫兵在黑暗里交接

branches.en: a village with no light in any window
branches.cn: 窗里没有一盏灯的村子

branches.en: a last train waiting under one lamp
branches.cn: 一盏灯下等候的末班车

branches.en: travellers hurrying aboard before the doors close
branches.cn: 赶在关门前上车的旅客

intro.en: Midnight joins the middle root to the word for night, and Latin built its own midnight phrase from exactly the same two elements.
intro.cn: midnight 把「中间」词根接到表示「夜」的词上，拉丁语用完全相同的两个成分造出了自己的「午夜」说法。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 套头毛衣；针织罩衫；跳跃者；跳高运动员；跨接线索
definition_en: a knitted garment pulled on over the head; also a person or animal that jumps, or a small wire used to connect points in a circuit
core_image: 一件从头上往下套的厚针织衫，或者一个正腾空跃起的人
scene: 山上的清晨很冷，她把自己裹得严严实实才出门。 She pulled on a warm wool jumper before stepping into the frosty morning.
sceneCN: 这里 jumper 是「套头毛衣、针织罩衫」（第 1 个义项：从头上套穿的针织衣物）；句意是她在清晨霜冷出门前套上一件厚羊毛衫。

pos.zh: 套头毛衣；针织罩衫（英式）
跨接线索；（美式）无袖连衣裙式外衣

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「跳；跃起」，jumper 加名词后缀 -er 表人
动词 jump 的动名词形式，义为「跳跃运动」
由 jump 加 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的；神经质的」

senses.title: A knitted garment pulled on over the head
senses.definition: a knitted piece of clothing, usually woollen, that you pull on over your head to keep warm
senses.definitionCN: 一种针织衣物，多为毛线织成，从头上往下套穿以保暖，即英式英语里的毛衣
senses.example: He wore a grey jumper over his shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 他在衬衫外面套了一件灰色毛衣。
senses.why: The noun is jump plus the agent suffix -er, and the garment is named after the action of jumping into it: you pull it over your head in one quick motion.
senses.whyCN: 名词由 jump 加表物/人的后缀 -er 构成；这种衣物因「一下套进去」像跳进去的动作而得名，故称 jumper。

senses.title: A person or animal that jumps
senses.titleCN: 跳跃者；跳高（跳远）运动员
senses.definition: a person or animal that jumps, especially an athlete who competes in jumping events
senses.definitionCN: 会跳跃的人或动物，尤指参加跳高、跳远等跳跃项目的运动员
senses.example: She is the best long jumper on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是队里最出色的跳远选手。
senses.why: This is the direct agent reading: jump plus -er names the doer of the action, following the same pattern as runner and swimmer.
senses.whyCN: 这是最直接的动作执行者含义：jump 加 -er 表「做跳跃动作的人」，与 runner（跑步者）、swimmer（游泳者）构词方式一致。

senses.title: A short wire connecting two points in a circuit
senses.definition: a small piece of wire with a connector at each end, used to link two points in an electronic circuit
senses.definitionCN: 两端带接头的短导线，用于在电路中把两个点临时连接起来，也叫跨接线
senses.example: Connect the two terminals with a jumper.
senses.exampleCN: 用一根跨接线把两个接线端连起来。
senses.why: The wire figuratively jumps across a gap in the circuit, so the jumping image is transferred to an object that bridges a space.
senses.whyCN: 这根线像是在电路的空隙间「跳过去」，跳跃意象被转移到跨越间隙的实物上。

senses.title: A sleeveless dress worn over a blouse (American)
senses.definition: in American English, a sleeveless dress worn over a blouse or sweater
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指罩在衬衫或毛衣外面的无袖连衣裙式外衣
senses.example: The school uniform includes a navy jumper.
senses.exampleCN: 校服包括一件藏青色无袖背心裙。
senses.why: In American usage the word drifted from the knitted top to the pinafore-style dress worn on top of other clothes, keeping the idea of a garment put on over another layer.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法从针织上衣漂移到罩在外面的背心式连衣裙，保留了「套穿在其他衣物外层」的核心意象。

senses.title: A loose outer garment or blanket-like cape (older use)
senses.definition: in older English, a loose outer garment or a blanket-like cape worn by women or workers
senses.definitionCN: 旧式英语中指宽松的罩衣或毯子似的披巾，多为妇女或劳动者所穿
senses.example: She wrapped a heavy jumper around her shoulders against the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一件厚实的罩衣裹在肩上御寒。
senses.why: This is the historical layer: the word first named a loose overgarment, and the modern sweater sense grew out of this earlier clothing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是历史层次：该词最初指宽松罩衣，现代「毛衣」义正是从这层衣物含义演化而来。

intro.en: Jumper comes from the verb jump plus the suffix -er. The clothing sense is generally traced to a loose overgarment first recorded in the seventeenth century, though the exact reason the garment was named after jumping is uncertain.
intro.cn: jumper 由动词 jump 加后缀 -er 构成。衣物义一般认为始于十七世纪记录的一种宽松罩衣，但这种衣物为何以「跳」命名，确切原因已不可考。

items.en: The verb jump first appears in English in the early seventeenth century; its deeper origin is uncertain, with proposed links to Germanic imitative roots expressing bouncing or thudding movement. Any earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 动词 jump 最早于十七世纪初见于英语；其更深的来源不确定，有观点认为与日耳曼语族模仿弹跳、砰然动作的拟声词根有关。更早的形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Jump emerges as a common verb for leaping, quickly replacing older native verbs such as leap in many everyday contexts.
items.cn: jump 作为表示跳跃的常用动词出现，在日常语境中迅速取代 leap 等更古老的本土动词。

items.en: Jumper is first recorded meaning a loose outer garment or cape. Why this garment was called a jumper is uncertain; a common suggestion is the idea of leaping or slipping into it quickly, but this remains conjecture.
items.cn: jumper 首次被记录为「宽松罩衣、披巾」义。这种衣物为何叫 jumper 已不可考；常见的一种解释是「迅速跳进去穿上」的联想，但这只是推测。

items.en: The agent sense, a person who jumps, develops naturally from jump plus -er, and gains a sporting flavour as athletics competitions formalise events such as the long jump and high jump.
items.cn: 表人的「跳跃者」义由 jump 加 -er 自然发展而来；随着跳远、跳高等田径项目正规化，这一含义带上体育色彩。

items.en: In British English, jumper narrows to mean a knitted sweater pulled on over the head, and becomes one of the most common everyday words for this garment.
items.cn: 在英式英语中，jumper 词义收窄为「从头上套穿的针织毛衣」，成为这类衣物最常用的日常叫法之一。

items.en: In American English the clothing sense instead refers to a sleeveless pinafore dress worn over a blouse, and a separate technical sense, a connecting wire in a circuit, appears in electrical usage.
items.cn: 美式英语中衣物义转指罩在衬衫外的无袖背心裙；电学用法中另出现「跨接线」这一技术含义。

note.en: Jumper looks and sounds close to several other words, and its meanings differ sharply between British and American English, so context matters.
note.cn: jumper 与若干词形相近的词容易混淆，且英式、美式含义差别很大，需结合语境判断。

entries.definition: to push yourself off the ground and into the air using your legs
entries.definitionCN: 蹬地跃起；跳；基础动词，是 jumper 的构词来源

entries.definition: nervous and easily frightened, as if always about to jump
entries.definitionCN: 紧张不安的；一惊一乍的；由 jump 加 -y 构成的形容词

entries.definition: a pair of wires used to connect one car battery to another
entries.definitionCN: 搭火线；跨接电缆，用于连接两辆车的电瓶，属复合名词

entries.definition: a knitted garment for the upper body; the common American equivalent of the British jumper
entries.definitionCN: 毛衣；美式英语中的常用对应词，与英式 jumper 第一义相同

entries.definition: a knitted top without buttons that you pull over your head
entries.definitionCN: 套头衫；与套穿毛衣义相近，强调无扣、从头上套穿

entries.definition: a sleeveless garment worn over a blouse, close to the American jumper dress
entries.definitionCN: 围裙式罩衣；背心裙，与美式 jumper 第四义相近

normalIntro.en: Use the base word jump and real word patterns to fix the meanings in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住基础词 jump 与真实构词、搭配规律，把各个含义钉进记忆。

normal.en: jump + -er = jumper: the doer of jumping, a person who jumps.
normal.cn: jump 加 -er 表人：跳跃者、跳高跳远运动员，这是最直白的构词。

normal.en: The sweater sense comes from the image of jumping into the garment: pull it over your head in one quick move.
normal.cn: 毛衣义来自「一下跳进去穿上」的画面：把衣服从头上快速套下。

normal.en: In Britain say jumper for a wool sweater; in America jumper is a pinafore dress — same word, different clothes.
normal.cn: 英国人说 jumper 指毛线衫；美国人说的 jumper 是无袖背心裙——同一个词指不同的衣服。

normal.en: In electronics a jumper jumps across a gap, connecting two points with a short wire.
normal.cn: 电子学里 jumper 是「跳过」空隙的短线，把电路中两个点连起来。

normal.en: Collocations to lock in: pull on a jumper, a chunky jumper, jumper cable.
normal.cn: 记牢这些搭配：pull on a jumper（套上毛衣）、a chunky jumper（厚毛衣）、jumper cable（搭火线）。

abstract.en: One motion, into the air: jump is a single explosive movement — the jumper rides that movement, whether person, garment, or wire.
abstract.cn: 一个腾空的动作：jump 是爆发性的一跳——无论人、衣服还是电线，jumper 都乘着这一跳。

abstract.en: Picture winter mornings: the thick wool jumper waiting by the bed, the first warm thing you jump into.
abstract.cn: 想象冬日清晨：厚毛线衫立在床边，是一天里第一个想钻进去的温暖之物。

abstract.en: A bridge in miniature: the jumper wire leaps a tiny valley of empty circuit board to make the connection.
abstract.cn: 微型桥梁：跨接线在电路板的空隙间一跃而过，完成连接。

examples.en: She knitted a blue jumper for her grandson last winter.
examples.cn: 去年冬天她给孙子织了一件蓝色毛衣。

examples.en: The young jumper cleared a personal best of two metres in the high jump final.
examples.cn: 这位年轻的跳高运动员在决赛中跳出了两米的个人最好成绩。

examples.en: It was so cold that he pulled on a thick jumper before going out.
examples.cn: 天太冷了，他出门前套上了一件厚毛衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「跳馍儿」——像跳进一碗热腾腾的馍汤里一样，把毛衣从头上一下套进去，暖意扑面。

root: jumper 由动词 jump（跳）加名词后缀 -er 构成。jump 的更早词源不确定，一般认为可能与日耳曼语族表弹跳动作的拟声词根有关，属重构形式；-er 是英语本土的施动/器物后缀， jumper 的「毛衣」义经由「跳进去穿上」的动作联想得名（此解释存疑，仅为常见推测）。

sensesIntro.en: From the single image of a jump, the word spreads to the garment you jump into, the person who jumps, the wire that jumps a gap, and older dress meanings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「一跳」这一个画面出发，词义延伸到跳进去穿的衣服、跳跃的人、跨越空隙的导线，以及旧式的罩衣裙装含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one leap — into a garment, over a gap, or off the ground
core.cn: 核心意象：一次腾跳——跳进衣服、跃过空隙、或蹬地而起

branches.en: The literal agent: an athlete or animal that jumps.
branches.cn: 最字面的施动者：跳跃的运动员或动物。

branches.en: The clothing line: from loose overgarment to knitted sweater.
branches.cn: 衣物一线：从宽松罩衣到针织毛衣。

branches.en: The American dress layer: sleeveless garment over a blouse.
branches.cn: 美式裙装层：罩在衬衫外的无袖背心裙。

branches.en: The technical transfer: a wire that jumps across a gap in a circuit.
branches.cn: 技术性转义：跨越电路空隙的导线。

branches.en: Everyday anchors: the two most common senses a learner meets first.
branches.cn: 日常锚点：学习者最先接触的两个高频义项。

intro.en: Jumper is built with a native English agent suffix, and its family shows how -er turns actions into doers and things.
intro.cn: jumper 由英语本土表人后缀 -er 构成；其词族展示了 -er 如何把动作变成「做动作的人或物」。

latinIntro.en: The jump- family is Germanic rather than Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the suffixes below are English and French borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: jump 词族属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，因此没有拉丁同源词可列；下面的后缀均为英语本土或法语借入的构词成分。

items.meaning: one who or that which does the action

items.example: start the car with jumper cables

items.meaning: athletic event of jumping over a bar
athletic event of jumping for distance
to start an engine with an external power source; to revive suddenly
sleeveless dress worn over a blouse

items.example: jump-start as spelled with a hyphen
items.exampleCN: jump-start 以连字符连接的写法

derivatives.zh: 由 jump 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的」
jump 的动名词，义为「跳跃」或「跳跃运动」

definition_zh: 安排；筹备；整理；排列；商定；改编（乐曲）
definition_en: to plan or organize something, to put objects in a particular order, to settle terms with someone, or to adapt a piece of music for performance
core_image: 把散落的物件一件件摆到各自该在的位置
scene: 婚礼前一天的教堂里，志愿者正把长椅和花束一一摆到合适的位置。 Volunteers spent the afternoon arranging chairs for the wedding.
sceneCN: 这里 arrange 是「整理、排列、布置」（第 2 个义项：把物件按顺序或位置摆好）；句意为「志愿者花了一下午为婚礼摆放椅子」。画面中有长椅、花束与来回走动的志愿者。

pos.zh: 动词：安排；筹备；整理；排列；商定；改编（乐曲）

derivatives.zh: 由 arrange 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「安排；布局；协议；改编曲」
由 arrange 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「安排者；乐曲改编者」
由前缀 re- 加 arrange 构成，义为「重新安排；重新排列」

senses.title: To plan and organize something
senses.definition: to plan and organize an event, meeting, or course of action in advance
senses.definitionCN: 预先计划并组织活动、会议或行动步骤
senses.example: They arranged a meeting for Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议安排在周五上午。
senses.why: The word first meant setting things in a row; planning is putting events in their proper row ahead of time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初表示把东西排成行；计划就是提前把一件件事排到它们该在的位置上。

senses.title: To put things in a neat order
senses.definition: to place objects in a particular order or position, often so that they look neat
senses.definitionCN: 把物件按特定顺序或位置摆放，通常是为了整齐好看
senses.example: She arranged the books by size, tallest on the left.
senses.exampleCN: 她按大小把书排好，最高的放在左边。
senses.why: This is the literal row: the hands move each object until the whole set lines up.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的「排成行」：双手把每件东西移动到位，直到整套都对齐。

senses.title: To settle terms with someone
senses.definition: to come to an agreement about the details of something with another person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或团体就某事的细节达成一致
senses.example: We arranged a loan with the local bank.
senses.exampleCN: 我们与当地银行商定了一笔贷款。
senses.why: Two parties are like two rows of items; the terms are settled once both sides line up.
senses.whyCN: 双方就像两排物件；当两边都对齐时，条款也就谈妥了。

senses.title: To adapt music for performance
senses.definition: to change a piece of music so that it can be performed by different instruments or voices
senses.definitionCN: 改写乐曲，使其能由不同的乐器或人声演奏
senses.example: The composer arranged the folk song for a small orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家把这首民歌改编成小编制管弦乐。
senses.why: Notes, like objects, are taken apart and set into a new order that suits the new performers.
senses.whyCN: 音符也像物件一样被拆开，再按适合新演奏者的方式重新排好。

intro.en: Arrange reaches English through French, but its root ring comes from Frankish, so the word carries a Germanic core inside a French shape.
intro.cn: arrange 经由法语进入英语，但它的词根「环、圈」来自法兰克语，因此这个词是法语外形包着日耳曼内核。

items.en: 「*hringaz」 is reconstructed as 'ring, circle', a shape word shared by several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 「*hringaz」被重构为「环、圈」，这是多个日耳曼语言共有的形状词。

items.en: Frankish 「*hring」 kept the ring sense, but how the meaning moved from a circle to a row is source uncertain.
items.cn: 法兰克语「*hring」保留「环」义，但意义如何从圆圈转到一排，来源存疑。

items.en: Arengier meant 'to put in a row, set in order'; the a- is a weakened form of Latin ad 'to'.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成行、摆整齐」；其中 a- 是拉丁语 ad「向」的弱化形式。

items.en: Arranger carried the row image onward and added the senses of settling a matter and fitting out a plan.
items.cn: arranger 延续了「排成行」的形象，又添上「谈妥事情」与「筹划」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century, first for placing things and later for planning.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，先用于摆放物件，后用于筹划事情。

items.en: The musical sense is the newest branch: notes are reordered just as objects were.
items.cn: 音乐义是最晚长出的分枝：音符被重新排序，正如当年的物件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close to arrange in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of planning and putting in order.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 arrange 接近的词；近义组收表示计划与整理的一类动词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to bring someone before a court to answer a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提审、传讯」，指带某人到法庭应讯。

entries.definition: An adjective used to emphasize a bad quality, as in arrant nonsense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，用于强调某种负面性质，如「十足的胡说」。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for a line of things, or for the extent covered by something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「一排、一系列」或「范围」，与 arrange 同源。

entries.definition: To bring people or parts together into a working whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或各部分组织成一个能运转的整体。

entries.definition: To make something ready for use or for an event.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物可供使用或为某件事做好准备。

entries.definition: To group things by kind or put them in order.
entries.definitionCN: 按种类分组或把东西排好。

entries.definition: To set a time and place for an event.
entries.definitionCN: 为某件事定下时间和地点。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a row of objects to plans, deals and music.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从一排物件走到计划、约定与音乐。

normal.en: Arrange begins with a row: things line up.
normal.cn: arrange 从一排开始：东西依次对齐。

normal.en: Arrange a meeting: events line up on a calendar.
normal.cn: 安排会议：事情在日历上一格一格排好。

normal.en: Arrange flowers: stems line up in a vase.
normal.cn: 插花：花枝在瓶里依次排好。

normal.en: Arrange a loan: two parties line up their terms.
normal.cn: 商定贷款：双方把条件排到一致。

normal.en: Arrange a song: notes line up for new instruments.
normal.cn: 改编歌曲：音符为新乐器重新排好。

abstract.en: One verb covers plans, objects, deals and music.
abstract.cn: 一个动词覆盖了计划、物件、交易与音乐。

abstract.en: The row image scales from a tabletop to a timetable.
abstract.cn: 「排成行」的形象从桌面一路放大到时间表。

abstract.en: Order is the thread that ties the senses together.
abstract.cn: 「次序」是把这些义项串起来的线。

examples.en: They arranged a meeting for Friday morning.
examples.cn: 他们把会议安排在周五上午。

examples.en: She arranged the books by size, tallest on the left.
examples.cn: 她按大小把书排好，最高的放在左边。

examples.en: The composer arranged the folk song for a small orchestra.
examples.cn: 作曲家把这首民歌改编成小编制管弦乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿让」——阿让把桌椅一排排摆好，又和客人谈妥了价钱：安排、整理、商定

root: arrange 经由古法语 arengier「排成行」进入英语，a- 是拉丁语 ad「向」的弱化形式，词根 rang 意为「一排、一列」，更早可追到法兰克语表「环、圈」的词。本义就是「把东西排成行」，由此长出三层意思：把事件排好是安排、筹备，把物件排好是整理、布置，把条款排齐是商定；音乐上的改编则是把音符重新排一遍。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow out of one gesture: setting things in a row. Events are rowed into a plan, objects into a layout, terms into a deal, and notes into a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都从一个动作长出来：把东西排成行。事件排成计划，物件排成布局，条款排成约定，音符排成乐谱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of objects being set one by one into their proper places.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排物件被一件件放到各自该在的位置。

branches.en: THE PLAN LINE: events are placed in their proper order ahead of time.
branches.cn: 计划线：事件被提前放到各自该在的位置。

branches.en: THE ROW LINE: hands move each object until the whole set lines up.
branches.cn: 排列线：双手把每件东西移动到位，直到整套对齐。

branches.en: THE TERMS LINE: two sides line up their conditions.
branches.cn: 条款线：双方把各自的条件排到一致。

branches.en: THE SCORE LINE: notes are reordered for new performers.
branches.cn: 乐谱线：音符为新演奏者重新排序。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: planning and tidying are the same gesture at different scales.
branches.cn: 日常线：安排与整理是同一动作在不同尺度上的表现。

intro.en: Arrange is a borrowed verb with a Germanic root, so its family is built by inflections, suffixes and the prefix re-.
intro.cn: arrange 是带日耳曼词根的借词，它的词族由屈折变化、后缀与前缀 re- 构成。

latinIntro.en: The root ring is Frankish rather than Latin, so there is no Latin layer to match here.
latinIntro.cn: 词根「环、圈」来自法兰克语而非拉丁语，因此这里没有对应的拉丁层。

items.meaning: to set in a row, put in order
items.example: They will arrange the room before the guests come.
items.exampleCN: 他们会在客人到来前把房间布置好。

items.example: She arranges the flowers every Sunday.
He is arranging the seats for the concert.
items.exampleCN: 他正在为音乐会摆放座位。

items.meaning: the past tense and past participle
items.exampleCN: 一切都在中午前安排好了。

items.meaning: the act or result of arranging
items.meaningCN: 安排、布局或协议这一结果
items.example: The arrangement of the desks pleased the teacher.
items.exampleCN: 课桌的摆法让老师很满意。

items.meaning: a person who arranges, especially music
items.meaningCN: 安排者，尤指乐曲改编者
items.example: The arranger rewrote the tune for strings.
items.exampleCN: 改编者把这首曲子改写成了弦乐版。

items.example: We had to rearrange the schedule after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，我们不得不重新安排日程。

items.example: They prearranged the meeting by email.
items.exampleCN: 他们通过邮件预先安排好了会议。

items.meaning: to disturb the order of something
items.example: The wind disarranged the neat rows of papers.
items.exampleCN: 风把排得整齐的文件吹乱了。

definition_zh: 娱乐；娱乐活动；招待
definition_en: shows, activities, or hospitality that amuse people or look after guests
core_image: 灯光、音乐与笑声组成的一整晚，还有摆满食物的餐桌
scene: 演出开始前，剧场经理说今晚的娱乐节目会持续到午夜。 Before the show began, the theatre manager said the evening's entertainment would last until midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 entertainment 是「娱乐节目」（第 1 个义项：使人开心的演出或活动）；句意：演出开始前，剧场经理说今晚的娱乐节目会持续到午夜。

senses.title: Shows and activities that amuse
senses.definition: films, music, games, or other things that give people pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 电影、音乐、游戏等给人快乐的事物
senses.example: The hotel offers live entertainment every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每晚都有现场娱乐表演。
senses.why: The noun names the things produced when people are entertained.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指人们被娱乐时所产生的事物。

senses.title: The act of entertaining guests
senses.definition: the activity of welcoming and looking after guests
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并照顾客人的活动
senses.example: Their hospitality was more than mere entertainment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的好客不只是表面的招待。
senses.why: The old hospitality sense of the verb survives in the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词古老的待客义项在名词中保留下来。

senses.title: A performance or event
senses.definition: a particular show or event that people watch for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 人们为消遣而观看的某场演出或活动
senses.example: The concert was good entertainment for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 这场音乐会对全家来说都是很好的消遣。
senses.why: One instance of amusing activity is counted as a piece of entertainment.
senses.whyCN: 一次具体的娱乐活动，就算作一件娱乐节目。

intro.en: Entertainment is entertain plus the noun ending -ment; the verb comes from Old French entretenir, to hold together.
intro.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 加名词词尾 -ment；动词来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Entretenir means to hold together and maintain.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen gives the base verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 提供基础动词。

items.en: The noun entertainment appears for hospitality and amusement.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，名词 entertainment 出现，表示招待与娱乐。

items.en: Public shows and the entertainment industry expand the word.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，公共演出与娱乐业扩展了这个词的用法。

items.en: Modern English uses entertainment for both shows and hospitality.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entertainment 既指节目，也指待客。

note.en: Entertainment is the -ment noun of entertain, and it sits near its family and near words for amusement and shows.
note.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 的 -ment 名词，与自身词族以及表示娱乐和演出的词相邻。

entries.definition: to amuse or receive guests
entries.definitionCN: 娱乐；招待

entries.definition: a person who amuses an audience
entries.definitionCN: 表演者

entries.definition: amusing and enjoyable
entries.definitionCN: 有趣的

entries.definition: the feeling of finding something funny or enjoyable
entries.definitionCN: 愉悦；消遣

entries.definition: a performance for an audience
entries.definitionCN: 演出

entries.definition: activity done for pleasure when not working
entries.definitionCN: 消遣；娱乐

normalIntro.en: Entertainment is entertain plus -ment, so it names the pleasure and the shows that result from entertaining.
normalIntro.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 加 -ment，指招待与娱乐所带来的快乐和节目。

normal.en: The ending -ment turns the verb into the activity or its result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动词变成活动或活动的结果。

normal.en: The entertainment industry is built on holding attention.
normal.cn: 娱乐业建立在「留住注意力」之上。

normal.en: Live entertainment means performers in front of a real audience.
normal.cn: live entertainment 指真人在观众面前表演。

normal.en: For entertainment is the phrase that names the purpose.
normal.cn: for entertainment 是说明目的的常用短语。

normal.en: Compare amusement: amusement is often the feeling, while entertainment is often the show.
normal.cn: 对比 amusement：amusement 常指感受，entertainment 常指节目。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre before the curtain rises, seats filling with chatter.
abstract.cn: 想象大幕拉开前的剧场，座位间满是交谈声。

abstract.en: Imagine a table cleared for cards and laughter after dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象晚饭后桌子被清出来打牌，笑声不断。

abstract.en: Think of a band tuning up while the lights dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光变暗，乐队正在调音。

examples.en: The hotel offers live entertainment every evening.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每晚都有现场娱乐表演。

examples.en: Their hospitality was more than mere entertainment.
examples.cn: 他们的好客不只是表面的招待。

examples.en: The concert was good entertainment for the whole family.
examples.cn: 这场音乐会对全家来说都是很好的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「entertain + ment」——把人留住、让人开心的那件事，就是娱乐；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）→ 中古英语 entretinen → entertain（招待、娱乐）＋ -ment → entertainment（娱乐；招待）。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers the feeling and activity of being amused, the old duty of looking after guests, and the concrete shows that produce pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词涵盖被娱乐的感受与活动、古老的待客职责，以及产生快乐的具体节目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an evening of lights, music, and laughter shared with others.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯光、音乐与笑声共享的一晚。

branches.en: Shows and games are the most visible form of entertainment.
branches.cn: 演出与游戏是最显眼的娱乐形式。

branches.en: Hospitality is entertainment in its oldest social form.
branches.cn: 待客是娱乐最古老的社交形式。

branches.en: A single performance is counted as one entertainment.
branches.cn: 一场演出可算作一项娱乐活动。

branches.en: The industry produces events, and each event is an entertainment.
branches.cn: 娱乐业生产活动，每场活动就是一项娱乐。

branches.en: A host's evening and a public show both aim at pleasure.
branches.cn: 主人的晚宴与公开演出都以快乐为目标。

intro.en: Entertainment is an English -ment noun built on the French-shaped verb entertain.
intro.cn: entertainment 是建立在法语形态动词 entertain 上的英语 -ment 名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is tenere, to hold; French entretenir keeps people together, and English adds -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 tenere（握住）；法语 entretenir 使人相聚，英语再加 -ment。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entretenir 开头。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Entertainment names the activity and its result.

definition_zh: 不断的；恒定的；忠诚的
definition_en: happening all the time without stopping, or staying the same in value
core_image: 钟摆一刻不停地摆动，幅度始终不变
scene: 夜里水管一直滴水，声音从没停过。 The constant dripping kept her awake.
sceneCN: 这里 constant 指「不断的」（第 1 个义项：持续不停发生）；句意是不断的滴水声让她睡不着。

senses.title: Never stopping
senses.definition: happening again and again without a real pause
senses.definitionCN: 反复发生而没有真正的停顿
senses.example: The constant noise made it hard to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的噪音让人难以入睡。
senses.why: A sound that never stops becomes a presence in the room.
senses.whyCN: 从不停止的声音，会变成房间里的一个存在。

senses.title: Staying the same
senses.definition: remaining at the same level or value
senses.definitionCN: 保持在同一个水平或数值上
senses.example: Keep the oven at a constant heat.
senses.exampleCN: 让烤箱保持恒定的温度。
senses.why: Science needs a number that refuses to move.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个不肯移动的数字。

senses.title: Loyal and faithful
senses.definition: remaining loyal to a person over a long time, a literary sense
senses.definitionCN: 长久地忠于某人，是较为书面的义项
senses.example: He remained her constant friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他始终是她忠诚的朋友。
senses.why: A heart that does not shift is also called constant.
senses.whyCN: 一颗不肯改变的心，也被称作忠贞。

intro.en: Constant comes from Latin constans, the present participle of constare, to stand firm, built from com-, together, and stare, to stand.
intro.cn: constant 来自拉丁语 constans，是 constare（站稳）的现在分词，由 com-（一起）与 stare（站立）构成。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and constare meant to stand firm together.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，constare 意为一起站稳。

items.en: Constans described a thing that kept its place and its nature.
items.cn: constans 描述守住位置与本性的事物。

items.en: Writers used it for people steady in loyalty.
items.cn: 作家用它形容忠诚不移的人。

items.en: French constant kept both the steady and the faithful senses.
items.cn: 法语 constant 同时保留稳定与忠贞两层意思。

items.en: English constant first described firm and unchanging things.
items.cn: 英语 constant 最初形容坚实不变的事物。

items.en: It now also names a fixed number in mathematics.
items.cn: 如今它也是数学里的一个固定数值。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin stand base or the same ending, and the meaning group names other words for something that does not stop.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语站立词基或相同词尾，近义组列出其他表示「不停」的词。

entries.definition: in a way that never really stops
entries.definitionCN: 不断地；老是

entries.definition: the quality of staying the same
entries.definitionCN: 恒久；忠贞

entries.definition: a clear difference between two things
entries.definitionCN: 对比；反差

entries.definition: regular and not likely to change
entries.definitionCN: 平稳的；稳定的

entries.definition: repeated many times over a period
entries.definitionCN: 一再重复的

entries.definition: continuing for a long time and hard to stop
entries.definitionCN: 持续的；顽固的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a point that refuses to move, then move to a fixed number and to a heart that stays loyal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个不肯移动的点开始，再到一个固定的数值，最后到一颗守着忠诚的心。

normal.en: Con- is together and stant is standing, so constant is standing still and refusing to budge.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，stant 是站立，constant 就是站定不动、不肯让步。

normal.en: A clock that ticks every second is constant, not fast.
normal.cn: 每秒滴答一次的钟是恒常，而不是快。

normal.en: Constant heat keeps a cake rising evenly.
normal.cn: 恒定的温度让蛋糕均匀地涨起来。

normal.en: The same friend in every season is a constant friend.
normal.cn: 每个季节都在的朋友，才是忠诚的朋友。

normal.en: What never pauses becomes part of the background.
normal.cn: 从不停下的东西，会变成背景的一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum swinging with the same width forever.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟摆永远以同样的幅度摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line across a graph with no slope.
abstract.cn: 想象图上一条毫无倾斜的直线。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp left on in a window all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窗里整夜亮着的一盏灯。

examples.en: The constant rain ruined the whole trip.
examples.cn: 不停的下雨毁了整个行程。

examples.en: Keep the room at a constant temperature.
examples.cn: 让房间保持在恒定的温度。

examples.en: She was a constant source of support.
examples.cn: 她始终是支持的来源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 constant 记成 con（一起）加 stant（站立）：始终站在原地不动，就是恒定的、不间断的。

root: 源自拉丁语 constare（com 一起 + stare 站立），本义是一起站稳，后指持续不断、数值恒定与忠诚不渝。

sensesIntro.en: From a sound with no pause, to a number that will not move, and finally to a heart that stays true.
sensesIntro.cn: 从毫无停顿的声音，到不肯移动的数字，最后到一颗始终如一的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum with the same swing, again and again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只以同样幅度一遍遍摆动的钟摆。

branches.en: The first sense is repetition so regular that it becomes background.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是规律到成为背景的重复。

branches.en: The second sense is a value that refuses to drift.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个拒绝漂移的数值。

branches.en: The third sense moves the same steadiness into loyalty.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把同样的稳定移到忠诚上。

branches.en: Both senses describe something you can measure and predict.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述可以测量和预测的事物。

branches.en: A constant number and a constant friend both keep their word.
branches.cn: 恒定的数值与忠诚的朋友都守着自己的承诺。

intro.en: Constant is built on Latin con-, together, plus stare, to stand, with the adjective ending -ant.
intro.cn: constant 由拉丁语 con-（一起）、stare（站立）与形容词词尾 -ant 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stand base stat- also appears in statue, stable and station.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的站立词基 stat- 也出现在 statue、stable 与 station 中。

items.meaning: the quality of staying the same
items.exampleCN: 她的坚贞让所有人惊讶。

items.meaning: a figure made to stand still
items.example: A bronze statue stood in the square.

definition_zh: 裸体的；赤裸的；无遮盖的；不加掩饰的
definition_en: not wearing any clothes; not covered by the usual layer; or stated openly without disguise
core_image: 层层遮盖被一层层剥去，最后只剩没有任何外物包裹的身体
scene: 清晨的海滩上空无一人，几个孩子把衣服堆在沙丘边，光着脚往浪里跑。 The boy ran naked into the cold water and came back laughing.
sceneCN: 这里是「裸体的、没穿衣服的」（第 1 个义项：身上没有任何衣物）；句意是男孩光着身子跑进冷水里，又笑着跑回来。图中可辨识物件：沙丘边的衣服、浅浪、光脚。

pos.zh: 裸体的；无遮盖的；不加掩饰的

derivatives.zh: 由 naked 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「赤裸；无遮盖」
由 naked 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「赤裸地；不加掩饰地」
由 naked 与 eye 复合而成，义为「肉眼观察的」

senses.title: Without any clothes on
senses.definition: not wearing any clothes, so that the whole body is open to view
senses.definitionCN: 没有穿任何衣物，整个身体都露在外面
senses.example: The child ran naked across the wet sand.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子光着身子跑过湿漉漉的沙滩。
senses.why: Old English nacod made a plain statement about the body: nothing is over the skin. That bare fact is the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nacod 只是对身体的直白陈述：皮肤上什么也没有盖。这个「什么都没有盖」的事实就是词的核心。

senses.title: Without the usual covering
senses.definition: not covered by the layer that normally protects or hides it, such as fur, leaves, paint or glass
senses.definitionCN: 缺少通常起保护或遮蔽作用的那一层，如毛、叶、漆或玻璃
senses.example: After the fire the hills stood naked in the morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 大火过后，山峦在晨光里光秃秃地立着。
senses.why: From a body without clothes the word moves to any surface missing its usual layer, because the picture is the same: a cover that ought to be there is gone.
senses.whyCN: 从没穿衣服的身体，这个词转到任何缺少惯常覆盖层的表面，画面其实一样：本该在那里的那层盖儿不见了。

senses.title: Open and undisguised
senses.definition: expressed or shown openly, with no attempt to hide it or make it softer
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达或显示出来，不做任何隐藏或软化
senses.example: He gave a naked account of how the money had disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不掩饰地讲了那笔钱是怎么不见的。
senses.why: When nothing covers a body, nothing covers a fact either, so the word lends its image to truth, greed or aggression shown without a disguise.
senses.whyCN: 身体无物遮盖时，事实也一样无所遮盖，于是这个词把自己的画面借给了不加伪装地摆出来的真相、贪欲或侵略。

intro.en: Naked comes from a Germanic adjective for a bare body, and it has widened from clothes to any missing cover or disguise.
intro.cn: naked 源自日耳曼语中形容光裸身体的形容词，后来从衣物扩展到任何缺失的覆盖物或伪装。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning bare or unclothed is generally accepted, and it is also the distant source of Latin nudus.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「光裸、无衣」的原始印欧语词根，它也是拉丁语 nudus 的远源。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective nakwadaz meant naked or bare, without the sense of a covering that had been removed.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形容词 nakwadaz 意为光裸，并不含「被脱掉覆盖物」的意思。

items.en: Old English nacod described a body with nothing over it, and it could also describe bare ground or a bare fact.
items.cn: 古英语 nacod 描述身上无物遮盖的身体，也可以形容光秃的地面或赤裸的事实。

items.en: Middle English naked kept the same sense, and its -ed ending was already part of the word rather than a past participle.
items.cn: 中古英语的 naked 保持原义，词尾 -ed 早已是词本身的一部分，而不是过去分词标记。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for uncovered surfaces and undisguised statements, giving such phrases as naked eye, naked flame and the naked truth.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指无遮盖的表面与不加掩饰的说法，于是有 naked eye、naked flame、the naked truth 等表达。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the shape of a past participle ending in -ed but have no link in origin; the near-meaning group collects words for a body or surface with nothing on it.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 -ed 结尾、外形相像但词源无关的词；近义组收表示身体或表面无物遮盖的词。

entries.definition: Cooked by dry heat in an oven; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在炉中用干热烤熟的；只是词尾外形相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Made to look real when it is not; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 把假的东西做得像真的；只是词尾外形相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Morally bad, or playfully mischievous; the -ed is pronounced the same way, but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上坏的，或淘气顽皮的；其中 -ed 读音相同，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Not covered by clothes or by the usual layer.
entries.definitionCN: 没有衣物或惯常覆盖层的。

entries.definition: Not wearing clothes, especially in art or a formal description.
entries.definitionCN: 未穿衣服的，尤用于艺术或正式描述。

entries.definition: Left open to view or to harm, with no protection.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露在视线或伤害之下的，没有防护的。

entries.definition: Not wearing clothes; a formal word for the same plain fact.
entries.definitionCN: 没穿衣服的；同一个朴素事实的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective for a bare body, and the -ed at the end is part of its history rather than a grammar ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中形容光裸身体的形容词，末尾的 -ed 属于它的历史，而不是语法词尾。

normal.en: Old English nacod is the direct ancestor, and the modern form keeps the same three consonants after the vowels shifted.
normal.cn: 古英语 nacod 是直接祖先，元音变化之后现代词形仍保留同样的三个辅音。

normal.en: The -ed is not a past tense ending: it has been inside the word since Old English, so naked does not mean having been naked.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ed 不是过去式词尾：它自古英语就在词里，所以 naked 并不表示「曾经裸过」。

normal.en: Naked eye means the eye with no lens or glass in front of it, which is the missing-cover sense at work.
normal.cn: naked eye 指前面没有镜片或玻璃的眼睛，正是「缺少覆盖层」这一义在起作用。

normal.en: Naked flame means fire with nothing around it, the same idea of a bare surface with no protection.
normal.cn: naked flame 指周围没有任何遮挡的火，同样是「裸露无防护」的意思。

normal.en: Nudus is the Latin word for bare, and it is a distant cousin of naked rather than the word that gave it birth.
normal.cn: nudus 是拉丁语中表示光裸的词，它是 naked 的远亲，而不是生出 naked 的母词。

abstract.en: Picture a body with every layer peeled away, and you have the single picture behind clothes, hills and truth.
abstract.cn: 想像一具被一层层剥去遮盖的身体，你就得到了贯穿衣物、山峦与真相的那一个画面。

abstract.en: A cover can be cloth, fur, paint or polite wording; the word treats all of them as the same thing when they are gone.
abstract.cn: 遮盖可以是布、毛、漆或客气的措辞；这个词把它们消失时的情形都看成同一件事。

abstract.en: Calling a fact naked says that no acceptable wording stands between the listener and the thing itself.
abstract.cn: 把一件事实称作 naked，等于说听者与事情本身之间没有任何可接受的措辞挡着。

examples.en: The child ran naked across the wet sand.
examples.cn: 那孩子光着身子跑过湿漉漉的沙滩。

examples.en: The planet is too faint to see with the naked eye.
examples.cn: 那颗行星太暗，用肉眼看不见。

examples.en: He gave a naked account of what had gone wrong.
examples.cn: 他毫不掩饰地讲了事情是怎么出错的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内壳的」——把外壳整个脱掉，露出里面；记住 naked 是赤裸的、无遮盖的。

root: 古英语 nacod（光裸的），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 nakwadaz，更早可追溯到原始印欧语表示「光裸」的词根，与拉丁语 nudus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body with nothing over the skin; the senses then extend that missing cover to surfaces and to facts stated without disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是皮肤上无物遮盖的身体；义项再把「缺少覆盖」扩展到表面，以及不加掩饰地说出的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: layer after layer of covering is stripped away until the body itself is all that remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层层遮盖被剥掉，最后只剩下身体本身。

branches.en: a child running into the sea with nothing on
branches.cn: 孩子身上什么也没穿，径直跑进海里

branches.en: a towel left on the sand beside a pile of clothes
branches.cn: 沙地上一条毛巾搁在一堆衣服旁

branches.en: hills stripped of grass after a fire
branches.cn: 大火之后被剥去草皮的山

branches.en: a wall with its paint gone, showing the bare brick
branches.cn: 墙面掉了漆，露出光秃秃的砖

branches.en: a sentence that hides nothing and softens nothing
branches.cn: 一句既不遮掩也不软化的话

intro.en: One Old English adjective, its English endings and compounds, and a Latin cousin that is related but not its source hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语形容词、由它而来的英语词尾与复合词，以及一个相关但并非其来源的拉丁远亲，共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin nudus and its verb nudare are generally treated as distant cognates of naked, related through the same older root rather than borrowed from each other.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nudus 及其动词 nudare 一般认为与 naked 同源，通过同一个更古老的词根相关联，而不是彼此借入。

items.meaning: adjective ending, not a past tense here
items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，此处并非过去式

definition_zh: 毁灭；毁坏；使破产；废墟；毁灭的原因
definition_en: to destroy or severely damage something, or the remains of a destroyed building
core_image: 一座塌了顶的老楼，断墙残垣立在原地
scene: 大火过后，整座房子只剩下焦黑的骨架。 The fire ruined the old wooden house completely.
sceneCN: 这里 ruin 是「毁坏」（第 1 个义项：彻底摧毁或严重损坏）；句意：大火把那座老木屋彻底毁掉了。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ous 后缀构成，义为「毁灭性的；导致破产的」
由形容词加 -ly 后缀构成，义为「毁灭性地；（价格）极高昂地」

senses.title: To destroy or damage badly
senses.definition: to spoil or destroy something completely or severely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底糟蹋或严重毁坏某物
senses.example: The flood ruined the harvest that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年的洪水毁了收成。
senses.why: A thing struck hard enough loses its shape and value at once.
senses.whyCN: 打击足够重，东西的形状与价值瞬间尽失。

senses.title: To make someone lose all their money
senses.definition: to cause someone to lose all their money or business
senses.definitionCN: 使人失去全部钱财或生意
senses.example: One bad investment ruined him financially.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔失败的投资让他倾家荡产。
senses.why: A person's fortune is a structure too, and it can collapse like a building.
senses.whyCN: 人的财富也是一座建筑，同样会像房屋一样坍塌。

senses.title: The remains of a destroyed building
senses.definition: the parts of a building that remain after it has been destroyed, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 建筑被毁后剩下的部分，常用复数
senses.example: Tourists walk among the ruins of the ancient temple.
senses.exampleCN: 游客们在古庙的废墟间穿行。
senses.why: What destruction leaves behind keeps the name of the destruction itself.
senses.whyCN: 毁灭留下的残骸，沿用了毁灭这个词本身的名字。

senses.title: The cause of destruction
senses.definition: the thing that causes someone's downfall or loss
senses.definitionCN: 导致某人垮台或损失的东西
senses.example: Gambling was the ruin of the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 赌博是整个家庭败落的祸根。
senses.why: The act of ruining is pinned onto the thing that did the ruining.
senses.whyCN: 「毁掉」这个动作被固定到实施毁灭的东西身上。

intro.en: Ruin comes from Latin ruina, a falling down or collapse, from ruere, to fall.
intro.cn: ruin 来自拉丁语 ruina（倒塌、崩落），动词词根 ruere 意为坠落。

items.en: Ruere means to rush or fall down, and ruina names the collapse itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ruere 意为冲落、坠下，ruina 由此指崩塌本身。

items.en: Old French carried the word as ruine, meaning collapse and destruction.
items.cn: 古法语将该词承袭为 ruine，指崩塌与毁灭。

items.en: Ruin entered English in the fourteenth century for the fall of buildings and of persons.
items.cn: 十四世纪 ruin 进入英语，兼指建筑与人身的倾覆。

items.en: Financial ruin became a standard use as commerce grew.
items.cn: 十六世纪起随商业发展，倾家荡产成为标准用法。

items.en: Ruins is now the usual word for ancient remains that tourists visit.
items.cn: 如今 ruins 是指称古迹残骸、供游客参观的常用说法。

note.en: Ruin has near-meaning words about destruction and look-alike words of different origin.
note.cn: ruin 的近义词集中在毁坏义场，形近词多属异源。

entries.definition: causing great damage or enormous expense
entries.definitionCN: 毁灭性的；（代价）高得倾家荡产的，ruin 的形容词形式

entries.definition: a small red-breasted bird
entries.definitionCN: 知更鸟，与 ruin 拼写部分相同，词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: costing so much that it destroys one's finances
entries.definitionCN: 贵得让人破产的，ruin 的副词搭配，强调代价之高

entries.definition: to put an end to something by breaking it completely
entries.definitionCN: 摧毁；消灭，强调动作的结果，不特指坍塌意象

entries.definition: to break a ship, building, or plan completely
entries.definitionCN: 使失事；破坏，多用于船、车与计划

entries.definition: to fall down suddenly; to fail suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 倒塌；崩溃，与 ruin 同属坠落意象，强调过程而非结果

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember ruin through falling and collapse.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕坠落与崩塌的记忆路径。

normal.en: RUIN sounds like RUIN DOWN: the roof falling in.
normal.cn: RUIN 读起来就像屋顶「轰然」砸下的声音，崩塌感十足。

normal.en: Latin RUERE means to fall: a ruin is what has fallen.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ruere 意为坠落：废墟就是倒下之后剩下的东西。

normal.en: Ancient ruins are walls left standing after the fall.
normal.cn: 古迹废墟是大楼倒塌后仍然站着的几面残墙。

normal.en: Debts pile up like stones until your finances collapse into ruin.
normal.cn: 债务像石块一样越堆越高，直到财务轰然倒塌。

normal.en: One wet phone in your pocket can ruin the whole day.
normal.cn: 口袋里进水的一部手机，就能毁掉一整天。

abstract.en: Watch a tower of blocks tip slowly and crash down.
abstract.cn: 看积木塔缓缓倾斜，然后哗啦倒塌。

abstract.en: See a garden drowned by one night of endless rain.
abstract.cn: 看一夜连绵大雨把整座花园泡烂。

abstract.en: Picture a broken bank building standing empty, its doorway open to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一座倒闭的银行空立街角，门洞朝天。

examples.en: The storm ruined our plans for a picnic.
examples.cn: 暴风雨毁了我们野餐的计划。

examples.en: They visited the ruins of the old city wall.
examples.cn: 他们参观了旧城墙的遗迹。

examples.en: His lawsuit nearly ruined the family business.
examples.cn: 那场官司几乎毁掉了家族企业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入阴」——大楼倒塌入于阴沟废墟之中；ruin 读音近似「入阴」

root: 源自拉丁语 ruere（坠落）的名词 ruina（崩塌），经古法语 ruine 于十四世纪进入英语；毁灭、破产、废墟诸义皆由「倒塌」意象生出。

sensesIntro.en: Ruin moves from falling down, to total destruction, to lost fortunes, to the remains and the cause.
sensesIntro.cn: ruin 从「坠落」出发，到彻底毁坏、倾家荡产，再到废墟残骸与祸根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something heavy falling down and breaking
core.cn: 核心意象：重物坠落、轰然坍塌

branches.en: A hard blow flattens what stood before.
branches.cn: 沉重一击把原本立着的东西夷平。

branches.en: A fortune is a building too, and it collapses the same way.
branches.cn: 财富也是一座建筑，同样会以同样的方式坍塌。

branches.en: What the fall leaves behind is called by the fall's own name.
branches.cn: 倒塌留下的残骸，以「倒塌」本身命名。

branches.en: The destroyer becomes the name of the destruction.
branches.cn: 实施毁灭者被固定为毁灭的代称。

branches.en: Ruins visited by tourists and gambler's ruin share one fall.
branches.cn: 游客凭吊的废墟与赌徒的破产，共享同一场坠落。

intro.en: Ruin builds its family around collapse and heavy loss.
intro.cn: ruin 的词族围绕崩塌与重大损失展开。

latinIntro.en: Ruin comes from Latin ruina, so it has Latin-rooted relatives.
latinIntro.cn: ruin 来自拉丁语 ruina，故有拉丁同根词。

items.meaningCN: 毁灭性的；代价极其高昂的
items.example: The war had a ruinous effect on trade.
items.exampleCN: 战争对贸易造成毁灭性影响。

items.meaning: in a way that destroys or costs too much
items.meaningCN: 毁灭性地；（价格）高得离谱地
items.exampleCN: 修缮费用高得让人破产。

items.example: The ruins attract visitors every summer.
items.exampleCN: 废墟每年夏天吸引众多游客。

items.meaning: to decay gradually into a broken state
items.example: The manor fell into ruin after the war.

items.meaning: to be the cause of someone's downfall
items.example: Drink was the ruin of him.

items.meaning: to spoil someone's plans or mood completely
items.meaningCN: 把某人的一天彻底毁掉
items.example: The flat tire ruined my day.
items.exampleCN: 爆胎毁了我一天的心情。

items.example: The fire caused irreparable ruin to the library.
items.exampleCN: 大火给图书馆造成无法挽回的损失。

items.example: We toured the ancient ruins at sunrise.
items.exampleCN: 日出时我们游览了古迹。

items.meaningCN: 被毁的；破产的；精疲力竭的
items.example: He returned home ruined by debt.
items.exampleCN: 他因债务缠身而破产还乡。

items.example: The town lay in ruins after the bombing.
items.exampleCN: 轰炸过后小镇沦为一片废墟。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 崩塌；倒塌（ruin 的直接来源）

definition_zh: 性的；性别的；有性生殖的
definition_en: relating to sex or sexual activity, relating to being male or female, or relating to reproduction involving two sexes
core_image: 两株花并立，花粉在风里从一朵飘向另一朵
scene: 这本书讨论性健康。 The book discusses sexual health.
sceneCN: 这里 sexual 是「性的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这本书讨论性健康。

senses.title: Relating to sex
senses.definition: relating to sex or sexual activity
senses.definitionCN: 与性或性行为有关的
senses.example: The book discusses sexual health.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书讨论性健康。
senses.why: This is the broad modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代宽泛的义项。

senses.title: Relating to gender
senses.definition: relating to being male or female
senses.definitionCN: 与男性或女性身份有关的
senses.example: Sexual differences appear early.
senses.exampleCN: 性别差异很早就显现出来。
senses.why: The adjective also describes division by sex.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也描述按性别的划分。

senses.title: By two sexes
senses.definition: relating to reproduction that involves two sexes
senses.definitionCN: 与涉及两性的繁殖方式有关的
senses.example: Many plants have sexual reproduction.
senses.exampleCN: 许多植物进行有性生殖。
senses.why: Biology uses the word for two-parent reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个词指双亲繁殖。

intro.en: Sexual comes from Late Latin sexualis, from sexus, gender.
intro.cn: sexual 源自晚期拉丁语 sexualis，来自 sexus（性别）。

items.en: Sexus meant gender.
items.cn: sexus 意为性别。

items.en: Sexualis meant relating to sex.
items.cn: sexualis 意为与性别有关的。

items.en: Sexual entered English from Latin.
items.cn: sexual 从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Sexual extended to activity and health.
items.cn: sexual 扩展到性行为与性健康。

items.en: Biology used sexual for two-sex reproduction.
items.cn: 生物学用 sexual 指两性繁殖。

note.en: Sexual is compared with similar-looking words and with words about the senses and intimacy.
note.cn: 把 sexual 与形近词以及表示感官与亲密的词作比较。

entries.definition: relating to the senses
entries.definitionCN: 感官的

entries.definition: following in order
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序的

entries.definition: real and existing
entries.definitionCN: 实际的

entries.definition: pleasing to the senses
entries.definitionCN: 感官享受的

entries.definition: very close and personal
entries.definitionCN: 亲密的

entries.definition: relating to producing young
entries.definitionCN: 生殖的

normalIntro.en: Sexual is the adjective of sex, covering gender, intimacy, and reproduction.
normalIntro.cn: sexual 是 sex 的形容词，涵盖性别、亲密与生殖。

normal.en: The clinic offers sexual health advice.
normal.cn: 诊所提供性健康咨询。

normal.en: Sexual equality is still debated.
normal.cn: 性别平等仍在讨论中。

normal.en: Sexual reproduction mixes two sets of genes.
normal.cn: 有性生殖混合了两组基因。

normal.en: The law protects sexual orientation.
normal.cn: 法律保护性取向。

normal.en: Sexual differences are not always social.
normal.cn: 性别差异并不总是社会造成的。

abstract.en: An adjective can turn a private fact into a public question.
abstract.cn: 一个形容词，能把私密的事实变成公共的问题。

abstract.en: Reproduction is life repeating with variation.
abstract.cn: 生殖，是生命带着变化重复自身。

abstract.en: The language of the body asks for honesty and care.
abstract.cn: 关于身体的语言，需要诚实与谨慎。

examples.en: The book discusses sexual health.
examples.cn: 这本书讨论性健康。

examples.en: Sexual differences appear early.
examples.cn: 性别差异很早就显现出来。

examples.en: Many plants have sexual reproduction.
examples.cn: 许多植物进行有性生殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: sexual 源自晚期拉丁语 sexualis，来自 sexus（性别），加形容词后缀 -al。

root: 源自拉丁语 sexus（性别），经晚期拉丁语 sexualis 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Sexual means relating to sex, to gender, or to two-sex reproduction.
sensesIntro.cn: sexual 意为性的、性别的或有性生殖的。

core.en: Belonging to the division of male and female.
core.cn: 属于男女两性的划分。

branches.en: Belonging to intimacy.
branches.cn: 属于亲密关系。

branches.en: Belonging to gender.
branches.cn: 属于性别类别。

branches.en: Belonging to two-parent reproduction.
branches.cn: 属于双亲繁殖。

branches.en: Intimacy and identity share an adjective.
branches.cn: 亲密与身份共用一个形容词。

branches.en: Gender and reproduction both need two.
branches.cn: 性别与生殖都涉及两方。

intro.en: Sexual is sex plus the adjective suffix -ual.
intro.cn: sexual 是 sex 加形容词后缀 -ual。

latinIntro.en: The Latin sexus, gender, also gave sexuality and sexism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sexus（性别）也孕育了 sexuality 与 sexism。

items.exampleCN: 人们的性取向各不相同。

items.example: The song has a sexy rhythm.

items.exampleCN: 这个笑话带有性别歧视。
